translations.idiomatic: 〈（Grandson Bian; Bian's grandson Qindao; Bian's clansman cousin Fan; Fan's disciple Shiliang）〉

translations.literal: Shigui, Fan's brother Shijing, Xu Yan
translations.idiomatic: Shigui, Fan's brother Shijing, and Xu Yan

translations.idiomatic: （Son Zun; great-great-grandson Chongrou; Xin Shaoxian; Wei Lang; grandson Zican）

sentences.zh: 宋隱，字處默，西河介休人也。

translations.literal: Song Yin, style Chumo, was a native of Jiexiu in Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yin, whose style was Chumo, came from Jiexiu in Xihe.

sentences.zh: 曾祖奭，祖活，父恭。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Shuang; his grandfather Huo; his father Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Shuang, his grandfather Huo, and his father Gong.

sentences.zh: 世仕慕容氏，位並通顯。

translations.literal: For generations they served the Murong clan, all holding prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family served the Murong, every man reaching conspicuous rank.

sentences.zh: 慕容俊徙鄴，恭始家于廣平列人焉。

translations.literal: When Murong Jun moved the capital to Ye, Gong first established the household at Lieren in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Jun moved the capital to Ye, Gong first settled the clan at Lieren in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 隱性至孝，專精好學。

translations.literal: Yin was supremely filial by nature and devoted himself to learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was profoundly filial by nature and threw himself into study.

sentences.zh: 仕慕容垂，位本州別駕。

translations.literal: He served Murong Chui as Recorder of the native prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served Murong Chui as Recorder of the native prefecture.

sentences.zh: 道武平中山，拜隱尚書吏部郎，積遷行台右丞，領選。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, Yin was appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat; over time he was promoted to Right Vice-Director of the mobile office, in charge of selection.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, Yin was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat, then promoted over time to Right Vice-Director of the mobile office with charge of selection.

sentences.zh: 以老病乞骸骨，不許。

translations.literal: He begged to retire on grounds of age and illness but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of age and illness and was refused.

sentences.zh: 尋以母喪歸列人，既葬被征，乃棄妻子匿于長樂，數年而卒。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to Lieren for his mother's mourning; after the burial he was summoned back, so he abandoned wife and children and hid in Changle, and died there several years later.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went home to Lieren for his mother's mourning; after the burial he was summoned again, abandoned wife and children, hid in Changle, and died there several years later.

sentences.zh: 臨終，謂其子經曰：「汝等苟能入順父兄，出悌鄉黨，仕郡幸而至功曹史，以忠清奉之，足矣。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he told his son Jing: "If you can treat your father and elders with obedience at home and show fraternal duty in the community abroad, and if in office in the commandery you are fortunate enough to reach the post of Merit Officer Recorder, and serve with loyalty and integrity, that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his son Jing: "If you can obey father and elders at home and show fraternal duty abroad, and in commandery service are lucky enough to become Merit Officer Recorder and serve with loyalty and integrity, that is enough.

sentences.zh: 不勞遠詣台閣，恐汝不能富貴，徒延門戶累耳。

translations.literal: Do not trouble yourself to go far to the central offices—for fear you cannot attain wealth and honor, you would only prolong the family's ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Do not trouble yourself to reach the central offices—you may fail to grow rich and will only heap ruin on the household."

sentences.zh: 若忘吾言，是死若父也。

translations.literal: If you forget my words, you will have wronged your father in death.
translations.idiomatic: If you forget my words, you wrong your dead father.

sentences.zh: 使鬼有知，吾不歸食矣。」

translations.literal: If ghosts have awareness, I will not return to eat with you."
translations.idiomatic: If ghosts have awareness, I will not return to share your food."

sentences.zh: 隱弟宣，字道茂，與范陽盧玄、勃海高允、博陵崔建、從子愔俱被征，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: Yin's younger brother Xuan, style Daomao, together with Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, Cui Jian of Boling, and his nephew Yin were all summoned and appointed as academicians in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's younger brother Xuan, style Daomao, was summoned along with Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, Cui Jian of Boling, and his nephew Yin and appointed Secretariat academicians.

sentences.zh: 後拜侍郎、行司徒校尉。

translations.literal: Later he was made Vice-Director and Acting Commandant-Validator of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Vice-Director and Acting Commandant-Validator of the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰簡侯。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Marquis Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he received the posthumous title Marquis Jian.

sentences.zh: 宣子謨，字乾仁，襲爵，卒于遼西太守。

translations.literal: Xuan's son Mo, style Qianren, inherited the title and died as Governor of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's son Mo, style Qianren, inherited the title and died as Governor of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 子鸞襲爵，位東莞太守。

translations.literal: His son Luan inherited the title and served as Governor of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luan inherited the title and held the post of Governor of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 鸞弟瓊，字普賢，以孝稱。

translations.literal: Luan's younger brother Qiong, style Puxian, was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's younger brother Qiong, style Puxian, was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 母曾病，季秋月思瓜。

translations.literal: When his mother had once been ill, in late autumn she longed for melons.
translations.idiomatic: Once when his mother was ill, in late autumn she craved melons.

sentences.zh: 瓊夢想見之，求而遂獲，時人異之。

translations.literal: Qiong dreamed he saw them, sought them, and obtained them; people at the time marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong dreamed of them, sought them, and found them; people at the time took it as a marvel.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 愔曆中書博士、員外散騎常侍，使江南。

translations.literal: Yin successively held the posts of Secretariat academician and Supernumerary Palace Attendant and was sent on a mission to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Yin served as Secretariat academician and Supernumerary Palace Attendant and was sent on a mission south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 爵列人子。

translations.literal: His title was Baron of Lieren.
translations.idiomatic: He held the title Baron of Lieren.

sentences.zh: 卒于廣平太守。

translations.literal: He died as Governor of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Governor of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 長子顯襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xian inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 顯無子，養弟子弁為後。

translations.literal: Xian had no sons and adopted his younger brother's son Bian as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had no sons and adopted his younger brother's son Bian as heir.

sentences.zh: 弁字義和。

translations.literal: Bian, style Yihe.
translations.idiomatic: Bian, whose style was Yihe.

sentences.zh: 父叔珍，娶趙郡李敷妹，因敷事而死。

translations.literal: His father Shuzhen married a sister of Li Fu of Zhao commandery and died because of the Fu affair.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuzhen had married a sister of Li Fu of Zhao commandery and died in the affair involving Fu.

sentences.zh: 弁至京師，見尚書李沖，因言論移日。

translations.literal: When Bian reached the capital he met Li Chong, Director of the Secretariat; their discussion lasted a full day.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian reached the capital he met Li Chong, Director of the Secretariat, and they talked the day away.

sentences.zh: 沖異之，退曰：「此人一日千里，王佐才也。

translations.literal: Chong was struck by him and said on leaving: "This man advances a thousand li in a day—talent fit to assist a king."
translations.idiomatic: Chong was impressed and said as he left: "This man covers a thousand li in a day—talent fit to assist a king."

sentences.zh: 」顯卒，弁襲爵。

translations.literal: When Xian died, Bian inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian died, Bian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 弁與李彪州裏，迭相祗好。

translations.literal: Bian and Li Biao were from the same commandery and treated each other with mutual esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Bian and Li Biao were fellow townsmen and held each other in mutual esteem.

sentences.zh: 彪為秘書丞，請為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: When Biao was Secretariat Director he asked that Bian be made Assistant Editor in the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao was Secretariat Director he had Bian appointed Assistant Editor in the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書殿中郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Palace Department of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director in the Palace Department of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝文曾因朝會次，曆訪政道。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen once, during an assembly, questioned him in turn on the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once, during court assembly, questioned him in turn on governance.

sentences.zh: 弁年少官微，自下而對，聲姿清亮，進止可觀。

translations.literal: Bian was young and his office low; he answered from below; his voice was clear and bright and his bearing admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Though young and low in rank, Bian answered from below in a clear, bright voice with admirable bearing.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善者久之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him at length.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 因是大被知遇，賜名為弁，意取弁和獻玉，楚王不知寶之也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he won great favor; he was given the personal name Bian, taking the sense of Bian He presenting jade while the King of Chu did not know its worth.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he won great favor; he was granted the personal name Bian, evoking Bian He presenting jade while the King of Chu failed to recognize its worth.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎兼員外散騎常侍，使齊。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice-Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Supernumerary Palace Attendant and sent on a mission to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice-Director of the Secretariat with concurrent Supernumerary Palace Attendant and sent on a mission to Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊司徒蕭子良、秘書丞王融等皆稱美之，以為志氣謇諤不逮李彪，而體韻和雅，舉止閑邃過之。

translations.literal: Xiao Ziliang, Minister of Education of Qi, Wang Rong, Secretariat Director, and others all praised him, saying his will and spirit were forthright though not equal to Li Biao's, while his tone and bearing were harmonious and elegant and his manner leisurely and deep, surpassing Biao's.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's Minister of Education Xiao Ziliang, Secretariat Director Wang Rong, and others praised him, saying his will and spirit were forthright though not equal to Li Biao's, while his tone and bearing were harmonious and elegant and his manner leisurely and deep—surpassing Biao.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice-Director of the Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice-Director of the Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 時散騎位在中書之右。

translations.literal: At that time the Palace Attendant post ranked above the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Palace Attendant post ranked above the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝文曾論江左事，問弁在南興亡之數。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen once discussed affairs south of the Yangtze and asked Bian about the number of years until the southern dynasty's fall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once discussed the south and asked Bian how long until the southern dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 弁以為蕭氏父子無大功于天下，既以逆取，不能順守，必不能貽厥孫謀，保有南海。

translations.literal: Bian held that the Xiao father and son had done the realm no great service; having seized power by rebellion, they could not preserve it by obedience, and would surely fail to secure their descendants or hold the southern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Bian held that the Xiao father and son had done the realm no great service; having seized power by rebellion they could not preserve it by obedience, and would surely fail to secure their descendants or hold the southern sea.

sentences.zh: 若物憚其威，身免為幸。

translations.literal: If creatures feared their might, they might escape with their lives—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: If others feared their might, they themselves might escape with their lives—that was all.

sentences.zh: 後車駕南征，以弁為司徒司馬、東道副將。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage campaigned south, Bian was made Acting Vice-Commander of the Ministry of Education and Eastern-route deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor campaigned south, Bian was made Acting Vice-Commander of the Ministry of Education and Eastern-route deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 軍人有盜馬靽者，斬而徇，於是三軍震懼，莫敢犯法。

translations.literal: When a soldier stole horse hobbles, he beheaded him and displayed the corpse; the three armies were awed and none dared break the law.
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier stole horse hobbles, he beheaded him and displayed the corpse; the three armies were awed and none dared violate the law.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎崔光薦弁自代，帝不許，亦賞光知人。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Cui Guang recommended Bian to replace himself; the emperor did not agree but also rewarded Guang for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Gentleman Cui Guang recommended Bian to replace himself; the emperor refused but also praised Guang for knowing men.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以弁兼司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Before long Bian was made concurrent Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bian was made concurrent Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 時大選內外群官，並定四海士族，弁專參銓量之任，事多稱旨。

translations.literal: At that time a great selection was made of officials within and without; the gentry of the four seas were all ranked; Bian alone handled the weighing of qualifications, and matters mostly pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time officials within and without were selected in a great ranking of gentry throughout the realm; Bian alone handled the weighing of qualifications, and matters mostly pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 然好言人之陰短。

translations.literal: Yet he loved to speak of people's hidden faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved to speak of people's hidden faults.

sentences.zh: 高門大族意所不便者，弁因毀之，至於舊族淪滯而人非可忌者，又申達之。

translations.literal: For great houses and clans he found inconvenient, he slandered them; for old families fallen into obscurity whose people were not to be feared, he spoke up for them.
translations.idiomatic: For great houses he disliked he spread slander; for old families fallen into obscurity whose people were not to be feared, he spoke up for them.

sentences.zh: 弁又為本州大中正，姓族多所降抑，頗為時人所怨。

translations.literal: Bian also served as Grand Rectifier of his native commandery and demoted many surnames and clans, winning much resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Bian also served as Grand Rectifier of his native commandery and demoted many clans, winning much resentment.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，尋遷右衛將軍、領黃門。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Regular Palace Attendant, then soon to Right Guard General with concurrent charge of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Palace Attendant, then soon to Right Guard General with concurrent charge of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 弁屢自陳讓，帝曰：「吾為相知者，卿亦不可有辭。

translations.literal: Bian repeatedly declined; the emperor said: "I know you as a friend—you must not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Bian repeatedly declined; the emperor said: "I know you as a friend—you must not refuse.

sentences.zh: 豈得專守一官，不助朕為政！

translations.literal: How can you hold to a single office and not help me govern!
translations.idiomatic: How can you cling to one office and not help me govern!

sentences.zh: 且常侍者，黃門之粗冗；

translations.literal: The Regular Attendant post is a rough, subordinate place in the Yellow Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendant is a rough, subordinate post in the Yellow Gate;

sentences.zh: 領軍者，三衛之假攝，不足空存推讓，以棄大委。

translations.literal: commanding the guards is a provisional assignment among the three guards—there is no room for empty modesty and abandoning a great commission."
translations.idiomatic: commanding the guards is a provisional assignment among the three guards—there is no room for empty modesty and abandoning a great commission."

sentences.zh: 」其被知遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor he enjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 孝文北都之選，李沖多所參預，頗抑宋氏。

translations.literal: In the selection for the northern capital, Li Chong took much part and greatly suppressed the Song clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the selection for the northern capital, Li Chong took much part and greatly suppressed the Song clan.

sentences.zh: 弁恨沖而與李彪交結，雅相知重。

translations.literal: Bian resented Chong and bonded with Li Biao in deep mutual esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Bian resented Chong and bonded with Li Biao in deep mutual esteem.

sentences.zh: 及彪之抗沖，沖謂彪曰：「爾如狗耳！

translations.literal: When Biao resisted Chong, Chong said to Biao: "You are like a dog!
translations.idiomatic: When Biao resisted Chong, Chong said to Biao: "You are like a dog!

sentences.zh: 為人所嗾。

translations.literal: Driven by someone else's hand."
translations.idiomatic: Driven by someone else's hand."

sentences.zh: 」及沖劾彪，不至大罪，弁之力也。

translations.literal: When Chong impeached Biao, he did not suffer the gravest penalty—Bian's doing.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong impeached Biao, he did not suffer the gravest penalty—thanks to Bian.

sentences.zh: 彪除名，弁大相嗟慨，密圖申復。

translations.literal: When Biao was stripped of his name, Bian sighed greatly and secretly plotted his restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao was stripped of his name, Bian sighed greatly and secretly plotted his restoration.

sentences.zh: 孝文在汝南不豫，大漸，旬餘日不見侍臣，左右唯彭城王勰等數人而已。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen fell ill at Runan and grew gravely ill, for more than ten days he did not see attending ministers; only Prince of Pengcheng Xie and a few others were at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen fell ill at Runan and grew gravely ill, for more than ten days he saw no attending ministers; only Prince of Pengcheng Xie and a few others were at his side.

sentences.zh: 小瘳，乃引見門下及宗室長幼諸人。

translations.literal: When he improved slightly he summoned the Gentlemen of the Gate and the elders of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: When he improved slightly he summoned the Gentlemen of the Gate and the elders of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 入者未能皆致悲泣，惟弁與司徒司馬張海歔欷流涕，由是益重之。

translations.literal: Those who entered could not all weep; only Bian and Acting Vice-Commander of the Ministry of Education Zhang Hai sobbed and shed tears, and the emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Those who entered could not all weep; only Bian and Acting Vice-Commander Zhang Hai sobbed and shed tears, and the emperor valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 車駕征馬圈，留弁以本官兼祠部尚書，攝七兵事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned to Maquan, Bian was left in his original post with concurrent Minister of Sacrifices, in charge of the seven military offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned to Maquan, Bian was left in his original post with concurrent Minister of Sacrifices, in charge of the seven military offices.

sentences.zh: 及行，執其手曰：「國之大事，在祀與戎，故令卿綰攝二曹。

translations.literal: On departure the emperor took his hand and said: "The great affairs of state lie in sacrifice and war; therefore I put you in charge of both offices."
translations.idiomatic: On departure the emperor took his hand and said: "The great affairs of state lie in sacrifice and war; therefore I put you in charge of both offices."

sentences.zh: 」弁頓首辭謝。

translations.literal: Bian bowed his head and declined with thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Bian bowed his head and declined with thanks.

sentences.zh: 弁劬勞王事，恩遇亞于李沖。

translations.literal: Bian toiled at the king's business and enjoyed favor second only to Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Bian toiled at the king's business and enjoyed favor second only to Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 帝每稱弁可為吏部尚書，及崩，遺詔以弁為之。

translations.literal: The emperor often said Bian could serve as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; when he died, the testamentary edict appointed Bian to that post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often said Bian could serve as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; when he died, the testamentary edict appointed Bian to that post.

sentences.zh: 與咸陽王禧等六人輔政，而弁先卒。

translations.literal: He was one of six, with Prince of Xianyang Xi and others, who were to assist the government, but Bian died first.
translations.idiomatic: He was one of six, with Prince of Xianyang Xi and others, who were to assist the government, but Bian died first.

sentences.zh: 年三十八。

translations.literal: He was thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈瀛州刺史，諡曰貞順。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Yingzhou; his posthumous title was Zhenshun.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Governor of Yingzhou; his posthumous title was Zhenshun.

sentences.zh: 弁性好矜伐，自許膏腴。

translations.literal: Bian was fond of boasting by nature and considered himself of the finest blood.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was fond of boasting by nature and considered himself of the finest blood.

sentences.zh: 孝文以郭祚晉魏名門，從容謂弁曰：「卿固當推郭祚之門。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, because Guo Zuo was a famous house of Jin and Wei, said casually to Bian: "You ought to yield place to the house of Guo Zuo."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, because Guo Zuo was a famous house of Jin and Wei, said casually to Bian: "You ought to yield place to the house of Guo Zuo."

sentences.zh: 」弁笑曰：「臣家未肯推祚。

translations.literal: Bian smiled and said: "My house is not willing to yield to Zuo."
translations.idiomatic: Bian smiled and said: "My house is not willing to yield to Zuo."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿自漢、魏以來，既無高官，又無俊秀，何得不推？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "From Han and Wei onward your house has had neither high office nor outstanding talent—how can you not yield?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "From Han and Wei onward your house has had neither high office nor outstanding talent—how can you not yield?"

sentences.zh: 」弁曰：「臣清素自立，要爾不推。

translations.literal: Bian said: "I stand on my own integrity and clarity; in any case I will not yield."
translations.idiomatic: Bian said: "I stand on my own integrity and clarity; in any case I will not yield."

sentences.zh: 」侍臣出後，帝謂彭城王勰曰：「弁人身自不惡，乃復欲以門戶自矜，殊為可怪。」

translations.literal: After the attendants left, the emperor said to Prince of Pengcheng Xie: "Bian's person is not bad, yet he still wants to boast of his house—it is very strange."
translations.idiomatic: After the attendants left, the emperor said to Prince of Pengcheng Xie: "Bian's person is not bad, yet he still wants to boast of his house—it is very strange."

sentences.zh: 長子維，字伯緒，襲父爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wei, style Boxu, inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wei, style Boxu, inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 為給事中。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant of the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 坐諂事高肇，出為益州龍驤府長史，辭疾不行。

translations.literal: For fawning on Gao Zhao he was sent out as Chief Clerk of the Dragon-Charger Office in Yizhou; he pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: For fawning on Gao Zhao he was sent out as Chief Clerk of the Dragon-Charger Office in Yizhou; he pleaded illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 太尉、清河王懌輔政，以維名臣子，薦為通直郎，辟其弟紀行參軍。

translations.literal: When Grand Commandant Prince of Qinghe Yi assisted the government, because Wei was a famous minister's son he recommended him as Direct Transmission Gentleman and recruited his younger brother Ji as Retainer.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Commandant Prince of Qinghe Yi assisted the government, because Wei was a famous minister's son he recommended him as Direct Transmission Gentleman and recruited his younger brother Ji as Retainer.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨政，委任元叉，恃寵驕盈，懌每以公理裁斷。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling took power she entrusted Yuan Cha, who grew arrogant with favor; Yi often judged him by public principle.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling took power she entrusted Yuan Cha, who grew arrogant with favor; Yi often judged him by public principle.

sentences.zh: 叉甚忿恨，思害懌，遂與維作計，以富貴許之。

translations.literal: Cha hated him greatly and plotted to harm Yi; he joined with Wei in a plan and promised him wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Cha hated him greatly and plotted to harm Yi; he joined with Wei in a plan and promised him wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 維見叉寵勢日隆，乃告司染都尉韓文殊父子謀逆立懌。

translations.literal: Wei saw Cha's power and favor growing daily and reported to Director of the Dye Works Han Wenshu and his son that they plotted rebellion to install Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei saw Cha's power and favor growing daily and reported to Director of the Dye Works Han Wenshu and his son that they plotted rebellion to install Yi.

sentences.zh: 懌被錄禁中。

translations.literal: Yi was taken and held in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was taken and held in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 文殊父子懼而逃遁。

translations.literal: Wenshu and his son, in fear, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu and his son, in fear, fled.

sentences.zh: 鞫無反狀，以文殊亡走，懸處大辟。

translations.literal: The interrogation found no sign of rebellion; because Wenshu had fled, he was sentenced to death in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: The interrogation found no sign of rebellion; because Wenshu had fled, he was sentenced to death in absentia.

sentences.zh: 置懌于宮西別館，禁兵守之。

translations.literal: Yi was placed in a separate lodge west of the palace and guarded by forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was placed in a separate lodge west of the palace and guarded by forbidden troops.

sentences.zh: 維應反坐，叉言于太后，欲開將來告者之路，乃黜為燕州昌平郡守，紀為秦州大羌令。

translations.literal: Wei should have suffered the penalty for false accusation; Cha spoke to the Empress Dowager, wishing to open the way for future informers, and Wei was demoted to Administrator of Changping commandery in Yanzhou and Ji to Magistrate of Daqiang in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei should have suffered the penalty for false accusation; Cha spoke to the Empress Dowager, wishing to open the way for future informers, and Wei was demoted to Administrator of Changping in Yanzhou and Ji to Magistrate of Daqiang in Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 維及紀頗涉經史，而浮薄無行；

translations.literal: Wei and Ji were both versed in the classics and histories, yet frivolous and without conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Ji were both versed in the classics and histories, yet frivolous and without conduct;

sentences.zh: 懌尊親懿望，朝野瞻屬。

translations.literal: Yi's honored kin and lofty reputation were looked to by court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's honored kin and lofty reputation were looked to by court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 維受懌眷賞而無狀構間，天下士人莫不怪忿而賤薄之。

translations.literal: Wei received Yi's favor and reward yet shamelessly sowed discord; men of learning throughout the realm all marveled and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei received Yi's favor and reward yet shamelessly sowed discord; scholars throughout the realm all marveled and despised him.

sentences.zh: 及叉殺懌，專斷朝政，以維兄弟前者告懌，征維為散騎侍郎，紀為太學博士、領侍御史。

translations.literal: When Cha killed Yi and monopolized court government, because the Wei brothers had earlier denounced Yi, Wei was summoned as Regular Palace Attendant and Ji as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and concurrent Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha killed Yi and monopolized court government, because the Wei brothers had earlier denounced Yi, Wei was summoned as Regular Palace Attendant and Ji as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and concurrent Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 叉甚昵之。

translations.literal: Cha was very intimate with them.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was very intimate with them.

sentences.zh: 維超遷通直常侍，又除洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei was promoted over rank to Direct Transmission Regular Attendant and also made Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was promoted over rank to Direct Transmission Regular Attendant and also made Governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 紀超遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: Ji was promoted over rank to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was promoted over rank to Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 紀字仲烈。

translations.literal: Ji, style Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, whose style was Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 初，弁謂族弟世景，言「維疏險而紀識慧不足，終必敗吾業」。

translations.literal: Earlier Bian had told his clansman cousin Shijing that "Wei is careless and dangerous while Ji's insight is insufficient—they will surely ruin my house."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bian had told his clansman cousin Shijing that "Wei is careless and dangerous while Ji's insight is insufficient—they will surely ruin my house."

sentences.zh: 世景以為不爾。

translations.literal: Shijing did not think so.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing did not think so.

sentences.zh: 至是果然。

translations.literal: By then it proved true.
translations.idiomatic: By then it proved true.

sentences.zh: 聞者以為知子莫若父。

translations.literal: Hearers said none knows a son like the father.
translations.idiomatic: Hearers said none knows a son like the father.

sentences.zh: 尚書令李崇、左僕射郭祚、右僕射遊肇每云：「伯緒凶疏，終敗宋氏，幸得殺身耳。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Li Chong, Left Vice-Director Guo Zuo, and Right Vice-Director You Zhao often said: "Boxu is vicious and careless; in the end he will ruin the Song house—lucky if he dies first."
translations.idiomatic: Director Li Chong, Left Vice-Director Guo Zuo, and Right Vice-Director You Zhao often said: "Boxu is vicious and careless; in the end he will ruin the Song house—lucky if he dies first."

sentences.zh: 」論者以為有征。

translations.literal: Discussants held there were signs of it.
translations.idiomatic: Discussants held there were signs of it.

sentences.zh: 後除營州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，以叉黨除名，遂還鄉里。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored the government she stripped Cha's faction of their names and Wei returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling restored the government she stripped Cha's faction of their names and Wei returned home.

sentences.zh: 尋追其前誣告清河王事，於鄴賜死。

translations.literal: Soon his earlier false accusation against Prince of Qinghe was pursued; he was granted death by edict at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his earlier false accusation against Prince of Qinghe was pursued; he was granted death by edict at Ye.

sentences.zh: 子春卿早亡，弟紀以次子欽仁嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chunqing died young; his younger brother Ji made his second son Qinren heir.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chunqing died young; his younger brother Ji made his second son Qinren heir.

sentences.zh: 欽仁，武定末為太尉祭酒。

translations.literal: Qinren, at the end of Wuding, was Libationer of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Qinren, at the end of Wuding, was Libationer of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 紀，明帝末為北道行台，卒晉陽。

translations.literal: Ji, at the end of Emperor Ming's reign, was Northern-route Mobile Vice-Director and died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, at the end of Emperor Ming's reign, was Northern-route Mobile Vice-Director and died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 子欽道。

translations.literal: His son Qindao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qindao.

sentences.zh: 欽道仕齊，歷位中山太守。

translations.literal: Qindao served Qi and rose to Governor of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Qindao served Qi and rose to Governor of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 長於撫接，然好察細事。

translations.literal: He was skilled at winning people, yet loved to scrutinize small matters.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at winning people, yet loved to scrutinize small matters.

sentences.zh: 其州府佐吏使人間者，先酬錢然後敢食。

translations.literal: The clerks and aides of his prefecture and office sent out as spies among the people had to be paid first before they dared eat.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks and aides of his prefecture and office sent out as spies among the people had to be paid first before they dared eat.

sentences.zh: 臨蒞處稱為嚴整。

translations.literal: When he arrived to take office he was called strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived to take office he was called strict and orderly.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為黃門侍郎，又令在東宮教太子吏事。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Vice-Director of the Yellow Gate and also ordered to teach the crown prince administrative affairs in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Vice-Director of the Yellow Gate and also ordered to teach the crown prince administrative affairs in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 時鄭子默以文學見知，亦被親寵。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Zimo was known for literary learning and also received intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zheng Zimo was known for literary learning and also received intimate favor.

sentences.zh: 欽道本文法吏，不甚諳識古今，凡有疑事，必詢子默。

translations.literal: Qindao had originally been a clerk versed in law and did not know antiquity well; whenever he had doubts he always consulted Zimo.
translations.idiomatic: Qindao had originally been a clerk versed in law and did not know antiquity well; whenever he had doubts he always consulted Zimo.

sentences.zh: 二人幸于兩宮，雖諸王貴臣莫敢不敬憚。

translations.literal: The two were favored in both palaces; even princes and honored ministers did not dare fail to respect them.
translations.idiomatic: The two were favored in both palaces; even princes and honored ministers did not dare fail to respect them.

sentences.zh: 欽道又遷秘書監，仍帶黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Qindao was again made Director of the Secretariat, still with concurrent Vice-Directorship of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Qindao was again made Director of the Secretariat, still with concurrent Vice-Directorship of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 乾明初，遷侍中，與楊愔同誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianming he was made Attendant and was executed together with Yang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianming he was made Attendant and was executed together with Yang Yin.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書、趙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Governor of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Governor of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 弁族弟穎，字文賢，位魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Bian's clansman cousin Ying, style Wenxian, held the post of Governor of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's clansman cousin Ying, style Wenxian, held the post of Governor of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 納貨劉騰，騰言之，以為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He bribed Liu Teng; Teng spoke for him and he was made Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed Liu Teng; Teng spoke for him and he was made Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 穎前妻劉氏亡後十五年，穎夢見之。

translations.literal: Fifteen years after Ying's former wife the Liu clan died, Ying dreamed he saw her.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years after Ying's former wife the Liu clan died, Ying dreamed he saw her.

sentences.zh: 拜曰：「新婦今被處分為高崇妻，故來辭君。

translations.literal: She bowed and said: "Your new wife has now been assigned as wife to Gao Chong; I have come to take leave of you."
translations.idiomatic: She bowed and said: "Your new wife has now been assigned as wife to Gao Chong; I have come to take leave of you."

sentences.zh: 」泫然涕流。

translations.literal: Tears streamed down.
translations.idiomatic: Tears streamed down.

sentences.zh: 穎且見崇，言之。

translations.literal: Ying soon saw Chong and told him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying soon saw Chong and told him.

sentences.zh: 崇後數日而卒。

translations.literal: Chong died several days later.
translations.idiomatic: Chong died several days later.

sentences.zh: 穎族弟鴻貴，為定州平北府參軍。

translations.literal: Ying's clansman cousin Honggui was a staff member of the Pacify-the-North Headquarters in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's clansman cousin Honggui was a staff member of the Pacify-the-North Headquarters in Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 送戍兵於荊州，坐取兵絹四百匹，兵欲告之，乃斬兵十人。

translations.literal: Escorting garrison soldiers to Jingzhou, he took four hundred bolts of silk from the soldiers; when the soldiers were about to report him, he beheaded ten soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting garrison soldiers to Jingzhou, he took four hundred bolts of silk from the soldiers; when the soldiers were about to report him, he beheaded ten soldiers.

sentences.zh: 又疏凡不達見令，律有梟首罪，乃生斷兵手，以水澆之，然後斬決。

translations.literal: He also was crude and did not understand the visible order; the law provided the penalty of exposing the head, yet he cut off the soldiers' hands alive, poured water on them, and then beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: He also was crude and did not understand the visible order; the law provided the penalty of exposing the head, yet he cut off the soldiers' hands alive, poured water on them, and then beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 尋坐伏法。

translations.literal: Before long he suffered execution by law.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he suffered execution by law.

sentences.zh: 時人哀兵之苦，笑鴻貴之愚。

translations.literal: People pitied the soldiers' suffering and laughed at Honggui's folly.
translations.idiomatic: People pitied the soldiers' suffering and laughed at Honggui's folly.

sentences.zh: 弁族弟翻。

translations.literal: Bian's clansman cousin Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's clansman cousin Fan.

sentences.zh: 翻字飛烏，少有操行，世人以剛斷許之。

translations.literal: Fan, style Feiwu, from youth had conduct and integrity; the world expected firmness of him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, style Feiwu, from youth had conduct and integrity; the world expected firmness of him.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時，除司徒左長史、河南尹。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's time he was made Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education and Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's time he was made Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education and Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 初，翻為河陰令，順陽公主家奴為劫，攝而不送。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fan was Magistrate of Heyin, a slave of Princess Shunyang's household committed robbery and was seized but not sent up.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fan was Magistrate of Heyin, a slave of Princess Shunyang's household committed robbery and was seized but not sent up.

sentences.zh: 翻將兵圍主宅，執主婿馮穆，步驅向縣。

translations.literal: Fan led troops to surround the princess's residence, seized her son-in-law Feng Mu, and drove him on foot to the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: Fan led troops to surround the princess's residence, seized her son-in-law Feng Mu, and drove him on foot to the county seat.

sentences.zh: 時正炎暑，立之日中，流汗沾地。

translations.literal: It was the height of summer; he was made to stand in the midday sun until sweat soaked the ground.
translations.idiomatic: It was the height of summer; he was made to stand in the midday sun until sweat soaked the ground.

sentences.zh: 縣舊有大枷，時人號曰彌尾青。

translations.literal: The county had long had a great cangue that people called "Mawei Green."
translations.idiomatic: The county had long had a great cangue that people called "Mawei Green."

sentences.zh: 及翻為縣，主吏請焚之。

translations.literal: When Fan became magistrate the chief clerk asked to burn it.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan became magistrate the chief clerk asked to burn it.

sentences.zh: 翻曰：「置南牆下，以待豪右。

translations.literal: Fan said: "Set it by the south wall to await the powerful."
translations.idiomatic: Fan said: "Set it by the south wall to await the powerful."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，有內監楊小駒詣縣請事，辭色不遜，翻命取尾青以鎖之。

translations.literal: Before long an inner attendant, Yang Xiaoju, came to the county on business with insolent words; Fan ordered Mawei Green taken to lock him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an inner attendant, Yang Xiaoju, came to the county on business with insolent words; Fan ordered Mawei Green taken to lock him.

sentences.zh: 小駒既免，入訴于宣武。

translations.literal: When Xiaoju was released he entered a complaint to Emperor Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoju was released he entered a complaint to Emperor Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 宣武大怒，敕河南尹推之，翻具自陳狀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu was greatly angered and ordered the Governor of Henan to investigate; Fan stated the facts in full.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu was greatly angered and ordered the Governor of Henan to investigate; Fan stated the facts in full.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿故違朝法，豈不欲作威以買名？

translations.literal: The edict said: "You deliberately violated court law—did you not wish to make a display to buy a name?"
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "You deliberately violated court law—did you not wish to make a display to buy a name?"

sentences.zh: 」翻對曰：「造者非臣，買名者亦宜非臣。

translations.literal: Fan replied: "The one who made it was not I; the one who buys a name should also not be I.
translations.idiomatic: Fan replied: "The one who made it was not I; the one who buys a name should also not be I.

sentences.zh: 所以留者，非敢施于百姓，欲待凶暴之徒如駒者耳。

translations.literal: The reason I kept it was not that I dared use it on the common people—I wished to await violent fellows like Xiaoju."
translations.idiomatic: The reason I kept it was not that I dared use it on the common people—I wished to await violent fellows like Xiaoju."

sentences.zh: 」於是威振京師。

translations.literal: Thereupon his authority shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his authority shook the capital.

sentences.zh: 及為洛陽，迄于河南尹，畏憚權勢，更相承接，故當世之名大致減捐。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang and then served as Governor of Henan, he feared and deferred to power, and received one another in turn; therefore his reputation in his day was greatly diminished.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Luoyang and then served as Governor of Henan, he feared and deferred to power, and received one another in turn; therefore his reputation in his day was greatly diminished.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈侍中、衛將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously made Attendant, Guard General, and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously made Attendant, Guard General, and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，重贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、尚書左僕射、雍州刺史，諡曰貞烈。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was again posthumously made General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat, and Governor of Yongzhou; his posthumous title was Zhenlie.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was again posthumously made General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Left Vice-Director of the Secretariat, and Governor of Yongzhou; his posthumous title was Zhenlie.

sentences.zh: 翻弟毓：字道和，敦篤有志行。

translations.literal: Fan's younger brother Yu: style Daohe, sincere and resolute with will and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Yu: style Daohe, sincere and resolute with will and conduct.

sentences.zh: 卒于太中大夫。

translations.literal: He died as Grand Master of Palace Service.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Grand Master of Palace Service.

sentences.zh: 子世良。

translations.literal: His son Shiliang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiliang.

sentences.zh: 世良字元友。

translations.literal: Shiliang, style Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang, whose style was Yuanyou.

sentences.zh: 年十五，便有膽氣。

translations.literal: At fifteen he already had courage.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he already had courage.

sentences.zh: 後隨伯父翻在南兗州，屢有戰功。

translations.literal: Later he followed his uncle Fan in Southern Yanzhou and repeatedly won merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed his uncle Fan in Southern Yanzhou and repeatedly won merit in battle.

sentences.zh: 行台、臨淮王彧與語，奇之。

translations.literal: Mobile Vice-Director Prince of Huaiyang Yu spoke with him and was struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Vice-Director Prince of Huaiyang Yu spoke with him and was struck by him.

sentences.zh: 魏朝以爾硃榮有不臣跡，帝將圖之，密令彧將兵赴洛。

translations.literal: The Wei court, because Erzhu Rong showed signs of disloyalty, planned against him; the emperor secretly ordered Yu to lead troops to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court, because Erzhu Rong showed signs of disloyalty, planned against him; the emperor secretly ordered Yu to lead troops to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 彧在梁郡，稱疾，假世良都督，令還南兗發兵以聽期。

translations.literal: Yu was at Liang commandery and claimed illness; he lent Shiliang his commandant's seal and ordered him to return to Southern Yanzhou to raise troops to meet the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was at Liang commandery and claimed illness; he lent Shiliang his commandant's seal and ordered him to return to Southern Yanzhou to raise troops to meet the deadline.

sentences.zh: 世良請簡見兵三千騎，五日必到洛陽，並陳三策，彧皆不能從。

translations.literal: Shiliang asked to select three thousand cavalry from the visible troops and reach Luoyang in five days, and set forth three stratagems; Yu could follow none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang asked to select three thousand cavalry from the visible troops and reach Luoyang in five days, and set forth three stratagems; Yu could follow none of them.

sentences.zh: 尋為殿中侍御史，詣河北括戶，大獲浮惰。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Attending Censor in the Palace and went to Hebei to register households, capturing many hidden and idle persons.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Attending Censor in the Palace and went to Hebei to register households, capturing many hidden and idle persons.

sentences.zh: 還見汲郡城旁多骸骨，移書州郡，悉令收瘞。

translations.literal: On his return he saw many bones beside Jijun city and sent letters to the commanderies and prefectures ordering them all collected and buried.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he saw many bones beside Jijun city and sent letters to the commanderies and prefectures ordering them all collected and buried.

sentences.zh: 其夜甘雨滂沱。

translations.literal: That night sweet rain poured in torrents.
translations.idiomatic: That night sweet rain poured in torrents.

sentences.zh: 河內太守田估贓貨百萬，世良檢按之，未竟，遇赦而還。

translations.literal: Governor of Henei Tian Gu had taken bribes of a million cash; Shiliang investigated but did not finish before an amnesty sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Henei Tian Gu had taken bribes of a million cash; Shiliang investigated but did not finish before an amnesty sent him back.

sentences.zh: 孝莊勞之曰：「知卿所括得丁，倍於本帳。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang comforted him saying: "I know the households you registered were double the original rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang comforted him saying: "I know the households you registered were double the original rolls.

sentences.zh: 若官人皆如此用心，便是更出一天下也。

translations.literal: If every official used his mind like this, it would be as if another realm had appeared under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: If every official used his mind like this, it would be as if another realm had appeared under heaven."

sentences.zh: 」其後遷殿中。

translations.literal: Afterward he was transferred within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was transferred within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 世良奏殿中主齊會之事，請改付余曹。

translations.literal: Shiliang memorialized that the Palace chief handled banquet affairs and asked that it be transferred to another office.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang memorialized that the Palace chief handled banquet affairs and asked that it be transferred to another office.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿意不欲親庖廚邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do you dislike working the kitchen yourself?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Do you dislike working the kitchen yourself?

sentences.zh: 宜付右兵，以為永式。

translations.literal: Give it to the Right Military Office and make that the permanent rule."
translations.idiomatic: Give it to the Right Military Office and make that the permanent rule."

sentences.zh: 」河州刺史梁景睿，枹罕羌首，恃遠不敬，其賀正使人，頻年稱疾。

translations.literal: Governor of Hezhou Liang Jingrui, a Qiang chieftain of Fuhan, relied on distance and was disrespectful; his New Year envoys for years claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Hezhou Liang Jingrui, a Qiang chieftain of Fuhan, relied on distance and was disrespectful; his New Year envoys for years claimed illness.

sentences.zh: 秦州刺史侯莫陳悅受其贈遺，常為送表。

translations.literal: Governor of Qinzhou Hou Mo Chen Yue accepted his bribes and often forwarded his memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Qinzhou Hou Mo Chen Yue accepted his bribes and often forwarded his memorials.

sentences.zh: 世良並奏科其罪。

translations.literal: Shiliang memorialized to convict them both.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang memorialized to convict them both.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，謂長孫永業曰：「宋郎中實有家風，甚可重也。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and said to Zhangsun Yongye: "Director Song truly has the family style—very much to be valued."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and said to Zhangsun Yongye: "Director Song truly has the family style—very much to be valued."

sentences.zh: 」後拜清河太守。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Governor of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 世良才識閑明，尤善政術。

translations.literal: Shiliang's talent and insight were clear and bright; he was especially skilled in the art of government.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang's talent and insight were clear and bright; he was especially skilled in the art of government.

sentences.zh: 在郡未幾，聲問甚高。

translations.literal: He had not been long in the commandery when his reputation rose very high.
translations.idiomatic: He had not been long in the commandery when his reputation rose very high.

sentences.zh: 陽平郡移掩劫盜三十餘人，世良訊其情狀，唯送十二人，餘皆放之。

translations.literal: Yangping commandery forwarded more than thirty robbers for arrest; Shiliang examined the facts and sent only twelve; the rest he released.
translations.idiomatic: Yangping commandery forwarded more than thirty robbers for arrest; Shiliang examined the facts and sent only twelve; the rest he released.

sentences.zh: 陽平太守魏明朗大怒云：「輒放吾賊！

translations.literal: Governor of Yangping Wei Minglang raged: "You casually release my bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Yangping Wei Minglang raged: "You casually release my bandits!"

sentences.zh: 」及推問，送者皆實，放者皆非。

translations.literal: When the case was pushed, those sent were all guilty and those released were all innocent.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was pushed, those sent were all guilty and those released were all innocent.

sentences.zh: 明朗大服。

translations.literal: Minglang was greatly convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Minglang was greatly convinced.

sentences.zh: 郡東南有曲堤，成公一姓阻而居之，群盜多萃於此。

translations.literal: Southeast of the commandery was Qudi, where the Cheng clan of Gong blocked the place and lived; many bandits gathered there.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast of the commandery was Qudi, where the Cheng clan of Gong blocked the place and lived; many bandits gathered there.

sentences.zh: 人為之語曰：「甯度東吳會稽，不曆成公曲堤。

translations.literal: People made a saying: "Better cross Dongwu and Kuaiji than pass Cheng Gong's Qudi."
translations.idiomatic: People made a saying: "Better cross Dongwu and Kuaiji than pass Cheng Gong's Qudi."

sentences.zh: 」世良施八條之制，盜奔他境。

translations.literal: Shiliang imposed eight regulations; the bandits fled to other regions.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang imposed eight regulations; the bandits fled to other regions.

sentences.zh: 人又謠曰：「曲堤雖險賊何益，但有宋公自屏跡。

translations.literal: People made another rhyme: "Qudi may be steep—what good are bandits? As long as Lord Song keeps them off himself."
translations.idiomatic: People made another rhyme: "Qudi may be steep—what good are bandits? As long as Lord Song keeps them off himself."

sentences.zh: 」齊天保初，大赦，郡無一囚，率群吏拜詔而已。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi there was a great amnesty; the commandery had not a single prisoner—the officials merely bowed to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi there was a great amnesty; the commandery had not a single prisoner—the officials merely bowed to the edict.

sentences.zh: 獄內厣魯生，桃樹蓬蒿亦滿。

translations.literal: Inside the prison even mice and peach trees were overgrown with wormwood.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the prison even mice and peach trees were overgrown with wormwood.

sentences.zh: 每日牙門虛寂，無復訴訟者，謂之神門。

translations.literal: Daily the gate of the yamen stood empty and still, with no more litigants; people called it the Spirit Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Daily the gate of the yamen stood empty and still, with no more litigants; people called it the Spirit Gate.

sentences.zh: 其冬，醴泉出於界內。

translations.literal: That winter sweet springs appeared within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: That winter sweet springs appeared within the borders.

sentences.zh: 及代至，傾城祖道。

translations.literal: When his replacement arrived the whole city saw him off on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When his replacement arrived the whole city saw him off on the road.

sentences.zh: 有老人丁金剛者，泣而前謝曰：「老人年九十，記三十五政。

translations.literal: An old man, Ding Jingang, wept and came forward to thank him: "This old man is ninety and remembers thirty-five administrations.
translations.idiomatic: An old man, Ding Jingang, wept and came forward to thank him: "This old man is ninety and remembers thirty-five administrations.

sentences.zh: 府君非唯善政，清亦徹底。

translations.literal: My lord was not only good in government—his clarity went to the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: My lord was not only good in government—his clarity went to the bottom.

sentences.zh: 今失賢者，人何以濟？

translations.literal: Now that we lose such a man, how can the people be saved?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that we lose such a man, how can the people be saved?"

sentences.zh: 」莫不攀轅涕泣。

translations.literal: None failed to cling to his carriage and weep.
translations.idiomatic: None failed to cling to his carriage and weep.

sentences.zh: 後卒于東郡太守，贈信州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he died as Governor of Dongjun and was posthumously made Governor of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died as Governor of Dongjun and was posthumously made Governor of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 世良強學，好屬文，撰《字略》五篇、《宋氏別錄》十卷。

translations.literal: Shiliang studied hard, loved composing text, and wrote five chapters of "Summary of Characters" and ten rolls of "Song Clan Separate Records."
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang studied hard, loved composing text, and wrote five chapters of "Summary of Characters" and ten rolls of "Song Clan Separate Records."

sentences.zh: 子伯宗，位侍御史。

translations.literal: His son Bozong held the post of Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bozong held the post of Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 性清退好學，多所撰述。

translations.literal: By nature retiring and fond of learning, he wrote much.
translations.idiomatic: By nature retiring and fond of learning, he wrote much.

sentences.zh: 至齊亡，不徙職，遂不入仕。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he did not change office and therefore never entered service.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he did not change office and therefore never entered service.

sentences.zh: 隋大業初，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye in Sui he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye in Sui he died at home.

sentences.zh: 世良弟世軌。

translations.literal: Shiliang's younger brother Shigui.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang's younger brother Shigui.

sentences.zh: 世軌幼自修整，好法律。

translations.literal: From youth Shigui disciplined himself and loved the law.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shigui disciplined himself and loved the law.

sentences.zh: 天保初，曆三尚書三公、二千石、都官郎中，兼併州長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he successively held the three Secretariat posts, the offices of two-thousand-bushel rank, and Director of the Ministry of Justice, with concurrent Long History of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he successively held the three Secretariat posts, the offices of two-thousand-bushel rank, and Director of the Ministry of Justice, with concurrent Long History of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 執獄寬平，多所全濟。

translations.literal: He held the prisons with leniency and fairness and saved many.
translations.idiomatic: He held the prisons with leniency and fairness and saved many.

sentences.zh: 為都官郎中，有囚事枉，將送，垂致法。

translations.literal: As Director of the Ministry of Justice there was a prisoner wronged in his case who was about to be sent off and nearly executed.
translations.idiomatic: As Director of the Ministry of Justice there was a prisoner wronged in his case who was about to be sent off and nearly executed.

sentences.zh: 世軌遣騎追止之，切奏其狀，遂免。

translations.literal: Shigui sent riders to pursue and stop it, memorialized urgently on the facts, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shigui sent riders to pursue and stop it, memorialized urgently on the facts, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 稍遷廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Vice-Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Vice-Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 洛州人聚結欲劫河橋，吏捕案之，連諸元徒黨千七百人。

translations.literal: People of Luozhou gathered planning to rob the He Bridge; officials arrested and tried them, implicating more than seventeen hundred Yuan partisans.
translations.idiomatic: People of Luozhou gathered planning to rob the He Bridge; officials arrested and tried them, implicating more than seventeen hundred Yuan partisans.

sentences.zh: 崔昂為廷尉，以為反，數年不斷。

translations.literal: Cui Ang was Vice-Director of the Court and treated it as rebellion; for years it was not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ang was Vice-Director of the Court and treated it as rebellion; for years it was not decided.

sentences.zh: 及世軌為少卿，判其事為劫，唯殺魁首，余從坐悉舍焉。

translations.literal: When Shigui became Vice-Director he judged the affair as robbery, executed only the ringleaders, and released all the rest who followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shigui became Vice-Director he judged the affair as robbery, executed only the ringleaders, and released all the rest who followed.

sentences.zh: 大理正蘇珍之以平幹知名，寺中語曰：「決定嫌疑蘇珍之，視表見裏宋世軌。

translations.literal: Chief Justice Su Zhenzhi was known for fair competence; within the office they said: "To decide doubtful cases, Su Zhenzhi; to see the inside from the outside, Song Shigui."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Justice Su Zhenzhi was known for fair competence; within the office they said: "To decide doubtful cases, Su Zhenzhi; to see the inside from the outside, Song Shigui."

sentences.zh: 」時人以為寺中二絕。

translations.literal: People of the time considered them the two marvels of the office.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time considered them the two marvels of the office.

sentences.zh: 南台囚到廷尉，世軌多雪之，仍移攝御史，將問其濫狀。

translations.literal: Prisoners from the Southern Terrace who reached the Court of Justice—Shigui acquitted many and then transferred authority to the Censorate to question their abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners from the Southern Terrace who reached the Court of Justice—Shigui acquitted many and then transferred authority to the Censorate to question their abuses.

sentences.zh: 中尉畢義雲不送，移往復不止。

translations.literal: Chief Commandant Bi Yiyun did not send them; the transfer went back and forth without stop.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Commandant Bi Yiyun did not send them; the transfer went back and forth without stop.

sentences.zh: 世軌遂上書極言義雲酷擅。

translations.literal: Shigui then submitted a memorial vehemently accusing Yiyun of cruelty and usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Shigui then submitted a memorial vehemently accusing Yiyun of cruelty and usurpation.

sentences.zh: 文宣引見二人，親敕世軌曰：「我知台欺寺久，卿能執理抗衡，但守此心，勿慮不富貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan summoned the two men and personally charged Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long bullied the Court—you can uphold principle and resist them; only keep this heart and do not worry about lacking wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan summoned the two men and personally charged Shigui: "I know the Terrace has long bullied the Court—you can uphold principle and resist them; only keep this heart and do not worry about lacking wealth and honor."

sentences.zh: 」敕義雲曰：「卿比所為誠合死，以志在疾惡，故且一恕。

translations.literal: He charged Yiyun: "What you have done truly deserves death; because your will is set on hating evil, for now I pardon you once."
translations.idiomatic: He charged Yiyun: "What you have done truly deserves death; because your will is set on hating evil, for now I pardon you once."

sentences.zh: 」仍顧謂朝臣曰：「此二人並我骨鯁臣也。

translations.literal: He then turned to the court ministers and said: "These two are both my bone-in-the-throat ministers."
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to the court ministers and said: "These two are both my bone-in-the-throat ministers."

sentences.zh: 」及卒，廷尉、御史諸系囚皆哭曰：「宋廷尉死，我等豈有生路！

translations.literal: When he died, prisoners throughout the Court and Censorate all wept: "When Vice-Director Song dies, how can we have a way to live!"
translations.idiomatic: When he died, prisoners throughout the Court and Censorate all wept: "When Vice-Director Song dies, how can we have a way to live!"

sentences.zh: 」贈光州刺史，諡曰平。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Guangzhou; his posthumous title was Ping.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Governor of Guangzhou; his posthumous title was Ping.

sentences.zh: 無子，世良以第五子朝基嗣。

translations.literal: He had no sons; Shiliang made his fifth son Chaoji heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons; Shiliang made his fifth son Chaoji heir.

sentences.zh: 翻弟世景。

translations.literal: Fan's younger brother Shijing.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Shijing.

sentences.zh: 世景少自修立，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: From youth Shijing disciplined himself; he was known for filial service to his parents.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shijing disciplined himself; he was known for filial service to his parents.

sentences.zh: 與弟道璵下帷讀誦，博覽群言，尤精經義。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Daoyu he studied behind curtains, reading widely, especially expert in classical meaning.
translations.idiomatic: With his younger brother Daoyu he studied behind curtains, reading widely, especially expert in classical meaning.

sentences.zh: 族兄弁甚重之。

translations.literal: His clansman cousin Bian greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman cousin Bian greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才上第。

translations.literal: He was presented as a xiucai and placed in the upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: He was presented as a xiucai and placed in the upper grade.

sentences.zh: 再遷彭城王勰開府法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Acting Legal Clerk in the Prince of Pengcheng Xie's opening office.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice promoted to Acting Legal Clerk in the Prince of Pengcheng Xie's opening office.

sentences.zh: 勰愛其才學，雅相器敬。

translations.literal: Xie loved his talent and learning and greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie loved his talent and learning and greatly esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 孝文甚嘉異之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen greatly praised and distinguished him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen greatly praised and distinguished him.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Acting Legal Clerk in the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Legal Clerk in the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 世景明刑理，著律令，裁決疑獄，剖判如流。

translations.literal: Shijing understood penal principle, compiled statutes, decided doubtful cases, and judged as if flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing understood penal principle, compiled statutes, decided doubtful cases, and judged as if flowing water.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of Sacrifices in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman of Sacrifices in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰每稱曰：「宋世景精微，尚書僕射才也。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie often said: "Song Shijing is subtle and refined—talent fit for Vice-Director of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Xie often said: "Song Shijing is subtle and refined—talent fit for Vice-Director of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 」台中疑事，右僕射游肇常以委之。

translations.literal: For doubtful matters within the Terrace, Right Vice-Director You Zhao often entrusted them to him.
translations.idiomatic: For doubtful matters within the Terrace, Right Vice-Director You Zhao often entrusted them to him.

sentences.zh: 世景既才長從政，加之夙勤不怠，兼領數曹，深著稱績。

translations.literal: Shijing was talented in government and, moreover, from old diligent without slackness; he concurrently held several offices and won deep praise for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing was talented in government and, moreover, from old diligent without slackness; he concurrently held several offices and won deep praise for achievement.

sentences.zh: 左僕射源懷引為行台郎。

translations.literal: Left Vice-Director Yuan Huai brought him in as Mobile Office Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice-Director Yuan Huai brought him in as Mobile Office Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 巡察州鎮，十有餘所，黜陟賞罰，莫不咸允。

translations.literal: He inspected more than ten provinces and garrisons; dismissals, promotions, rewards, and punishments all won approval.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected more than ten provinces and garrisons; dismissals, promotions, rewards, and punishments all won approval.

sentences.zh: 遷七鎮，別置諸戍，明設亭候，以備不虞。

translations.literal: He moved the seven garrisons, separately established the various posts, and clearly set watch-towers to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the seven garrisons, separately established the various posts, and clearly set watch-towers to guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 懷大相委重，還，薦之宣武，以為不減李沖。

translations.literal: Huai greatly entrusted him; on his return he recommended him to Emperor Xuanwu, saying he was not inferior to Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Huai greatly entrusted him; on his return he recommended him to Emperor Xuanwu, saying he was not inferior to Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕亦聞之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have also heard of him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I have also heard of him."

sentences.zh: 」後為伏波將軍，行榮陽太守，鄭氏豪橫，號為難制。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Subdues the Waves and Acting Governor of Xingyang; the Zheng clan of Zheng was overbearing and called hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made General Who Subdues the Waves and Acting Governor of Xingyang; the Zheng clan of Zheng was overbearing and called hard to control.

sentences.zh: 濟州刺史鄭尚弟遠慶，先為苑陵令，多所受納，百姓患之。

translations.literal: Governor of Jizhou Zheng Shang's younger brother Yuanqing had earlier been Magistrate of Yuanling and took many bribes; the people suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Jizhou Zheng Shang's younger brother Yuanqing had earlier been Magistrate of Yuanling and took many bribes; the people suffered from him.

sentences.zh: 而世景下車，召而誡之。

translations.literal: When Shijing took his post he summoned and admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shijing took his post he summoned and admonished him.

sentences.zh: 遠慶行意自若，世景繩之以法。

translations.literal: Yuanqing acted as he pleased; Shijing bound him by law.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing acted as he pleased; Shijing bound him by law.

sentences.zh: 遠慶懼，棄官亡走。

translations.literal: Yuanqing was afraid, abandoned his office, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing was afraid, abandoned his office, and fled.

sentences.zh: 於是屬縣畏威，莫不改肅。

translations.literal: Thereupon the subordinate counties feared his authority and none failed to reform and become solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the subordinate counties feared his authority and none failed to reform and become solemn.

sentences.zh: 終日坐於査事，未嘗寢息。

translations.literal: He sat all day investigating affairs and never rested.
translations.idiomatic: He sat all day investigating affairs and never rested.

sentences.zh: 人間之事，巨細必知。

translations.literal: Matters among the people, great or small, he always knew.
translations.idiomatic: Matters among the people, great or small, he always knew.

sentences.zh: 發奸擿伏，有若神明。

translations.literal: Exposing wrong and plucking out the hidden, he was like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Exposing wrong and plucking out the hidden, he was like a spirit.

sentences.zh: 嘗有一吏，休滿還郡，食人雞豚。

translations.literal: Once there was a clerk whose term ended and who returned to the commandery and ate someone's chickens and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: Once there was a clerk whose term ended and who returned to the commandery and ate someone's chickens and pigs.

sentences.zh: 又有一干，受人一帽，又食二雞。

translations.literal: There was also a runner who accepted one hat from someone and also ate two chickens.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a runner who accepted one hat from someone and also ate two chickens.

sentences.zh: 世景叱而告之，吏、幹叩頭伏罪。

translations.literal: Shijing shouted and told them; the clerk and runner knocked their heads and confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing shouted and told them; the clerk and runner knocked their heads and confessed guilt.

sentences.zh: 於是上下震悚，莫敢犯禁。

translations.literal: Thereupon above and below were awed and none dared violate the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon above and below were awed and none dared violate the prohibition.

sentences.zh: 坐弟道璵事除名。

translations.literal: He was stripped of his name because of his younger brother Daoyu's affair.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his name because of his younger brother Daoyu's affair.

sentences.zh: 世景友于之性，過絕於人，及道璵死，哭之，酸感行路。

translations.literal: Shijing's fraternal affection surpassed others; when Daoyu died he wept for him with grief that moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing's fraternal affection surpassed others; when Daoyu died he wept for him with grief that moved passersby on the road.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，母喪，遂不勝哀而卒。

translations.literal: More than a year later, in his mother's mourning, he could not bear the grief and died.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, in his mother's mourning, he could not bear the grief and died.

sentences.zh: 世景曾撰《晉書》，竟未得就。

translations.literal: Shijing once compiled a "History of Jin" but never finished it.
translations.idiomatic: Shijing once compiled a "History of Jin" but never finished it.

sentences.zh: 遺腹子季儒，位太學博士。

translations.literal: His posthumous son Jiru held the post of Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous son Jiru held the post of Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 曾至譙、宋間，為文吊嵇康，甚有理致。

translations.literal: He once went to Qiao and Song and wrote a text mourning Ji Kang with very sound reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: He once went to Qiao and Song and wrote a text mourning Ji Kang with very sound reasoning.

sentences.zh: 後夜寢室壞，壓而殞，時人悼傷惜之。

translations.literal: Later his bedroom collapsed and crushed him to death; people mourned and pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Later his bedroom collapsed and crushed him to death; people mourned and pitied him.

sentences.zh: 道璵少而敏俊，自太學博士轉京兆王愉法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: Daoyu from youth was clever and handsome; from Erudite of the Imperial Academy he was transferred to Acting Legal Clerk in Prince of Jingzhao Yu's opening office.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu from youth was clever and handsome; from Erudite of the Imperial Academy he was transferred to Acting Legal Clerk in Prince of Jingzhao Yu's opening office.

sentences.zh: 坐愉反得罪。

translations.literal: He was punished because of Yu's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished because of Yu's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 作詩及輓歌詞寄之朋親，以見冤痛。

translations.literal: He composed poems and elegiac verses and sent them to friends and kin to show his wrongful suffering.
translations.idiomatic: He composed poems and elegiac verses and sent them to friends and kin to show his wrongful suffering.

sentences.zh: 道璵又曾贈著作郎張始均詩，其末章云：「子深懷璧憂，餘有當門病。

translations.literal: Daoyu also once gave a poem to Editor Zhang Shijun; its final stanza said: "Zi bears the worry of cherishing a jade; I have the sickness of standing in the gate."
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu also once gave a poem to Editor Zhang Shijun; its final stanza said: "Zi bears the worry of cherishing a jade; I have the sickness of standing in the gate."

sentences.zh: 」道璵既不免難，始均亦遇世禍，時咸怪之。

translations.literal: When Daoyu could not escape disaster, Shijun also met worldly calamity; people at the time all found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoyu could not escape disaster, Shijun also met worldly calamity; people at the time all found it strange.

sentences.zh: 道璵從孫孝王，學涉，亦好緝綴文藻。

translations.literal: Daoyu's distant nephew Xiaowang was learned and also loved compiling literary ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu's distant nephew Xiaowang was learned and also loved compiling literary ornament.

sentences.zh: 形貌矬陋而好臧否人物，時論甚疾之。

translations.literal: His appearance was short and ugly and he loved to judge people; opinion greatly disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: His appearance was short and ugly and he loved to judge people; opinion greatly disliked him.

sentences.zh: 為北平王文學。

translations.literal: He was Literary Scholar to Prince of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was Literary Scholar to Prince of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 求入文林館不遂，因非毀朝士，撰《朝士別錄》二十卷。

translations.literal: He sought entry into the Forest of Literature and failed; he therefore slandered court gentlemen and compiled twenty rolls of "Separate Records of Court Gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: He sought entry into the Forest of Literature and failed; he therefore slandered court gentlemen and compiled twenty rolls of "Separate Records of Court Gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 會周武滅齊，改為《關東風俗傳》，更廣聞見，勒成三十卷以上之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou destroyed Qi he changed the title to "Customs of the Eastern Pass" and broadened what he had heard and seen, compiling more than thirty rolls and presenting them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou destroyed Qi he changed the title to "Customs of the Eastern Pass" and broadened what he had heard and seen, compiling more than thirty rolls and presenting them.

sentences.zh: 言多妄謬，篇第冗雜，無著述體。

translations.literal: The words were mostly false and absurd, the sections redundant and messy, without the form of a composition.
translations.idiomatic: The words were mostly false and absurd, the sections redundant and messy, without the form of a composition.

sentences.zh: 周大象末。

translations.literal: At the end of the Great Elephant reign in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Great Elephant reign in Zhou.

sentences.zh: 預尉迥事，誅死。

translations.literal: He took part in Wei Jiong's affair and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in Wei Jiong's affair and was executed.

sentences.zh: 許彥，字道謨，高陽新城人也。

translations.literal: Xu Yan, style Daomo, was a native of Xincheng in Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan, whose style was Daomo, came from Xincheng in Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 祖茂，仕慕容氏高陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mao served the Murong as Governor of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mao served the Murong as Governor of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 彥少孤貧，好讀書，從沙門法睿受《易》。

translations.literal: Yan from youth was orphaned and poor, loved reading, and studied the "Changes" under the monk Fawei.
translations.idiomatic: Yan from youth was orphaned and poor, loved reading, and studied the "Changes" under the monk Fawei.

sentences.zh: 太武征令卜筮，頻驗，遂在左右，參與謀議。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu campaigned he was ordered to perform divination; he was repeatedly verified and thus remained at the emperor's side, taking part in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu campaigned he was ordered to perform divination; he was repeatedly verified and thus remained at the emperor's side, taking part in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 彥質厚慎密，與人言，不及內事，帝以此益親待之。

translations.literal: Yan was plain, thick, and cautious; in speaking with others he did not touch inner affairs; the emperor for this treated him all the more intimately.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was plain, thick, and cautious; in speaking with others he did not touch inner affairs; the emperor for this treated him all the more intimately.

sentences.zh: 賜爵武昌公，拜相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was given the title Duke of Wuchang and made Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the title Duke of Wuchang and made Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州受納，多違法度，詔書切讓之，然以彥腹心近臣，弗之罪也。

translations.literal: In the province he accepted bribes and often violated the law; edicts sternly reproved him, yet because Yan was a close minister at the emperor's heart he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he accepted bribes and often violated the law; edicts sternly reproved him, yet because Yan was a close minister at the emperor's heart he was not punished.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡宣公。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Duke Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous title was Duke Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子熙襲。

translations.literal: His son Xi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi inherited.

sentences.zh: 熙卒，子安仁襲。

translations.literal: When Xi died, his son Anren inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi died, his son Anren inherited.

sentences.zh: 安仁卒，子元康襲，降爵為侯。

translations.literal: When Anren died, his son Yuankang inherited; the title was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Anren died, his son Yuankang inherited; the title was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 熙弟宗之，歷位殿中尚書、定州刺史，封潁川公。

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother Zongzhi held in succession Palace Attendant Within the Hall and Governor of Dingzhou and was enfeoffed Duke of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Zongzhi served as Palace Attendant Within the Hall and Governor of Dingzhou and was made Duke of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 受敕討丁零。

translations.literal: He received an edict to campaign against the Dingling.
