translations.idiomatic: Ordered to campaign against the Dingling.

sentences.zh: 既平，宗之因循郡縣，求取不節。

translations.literal: Once pacified, Zongzhi lingered through the commanderies and districts, demanding gifts without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: After victory Zongzhi toured the counties demanding bribes without limit.

sentences.zh: 深澤人馬超譭謗宗之，宗之怒，毆殺超。

translations.literal: Ma Chao of Shenze slandered Zongzhi; Zongzhi in anger beat and killed Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao of Shenze maligned him; Zongzhi beat him to death in a rage.

sentences.zh: 超家人告狀，宗之上超謗訕朝政。

translations.literal: Chao's family lodged a complaint; Zongzhi charged Chao with slandering the court.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's kin sued; Zongzhi accused Chao of maligning the throne.

sentences.zh: 文成聞之曰：「此必宗之懼罪誣超。

translations.literal: Wencheng heard of it and said: "This must be Zongzhi, fearing guilt, framing Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng said: "Zongzhi must fear punishment and is framing Chao."

sentences.zh: 」案驗果然，遂斬於都市。

translations.literal: " Investigation verified it was so, and he was beheaded in the market.
translations.idiomatic: The inquiry proved it; he was beheaded in the market.

sentences.zh: 元康弟護，州主簿。

translations.literal: Yuankang's younger brother Hu was a provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang's younger brother Hu was a provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 子恂，字伯禮，頗有業尚，閨門雍睦，三世同居，吏部尚書李神俊常稱其家風。

translations.literal: His son Xun, styled Bolü, had considerable scholarly ambition; the household was harmonious and three generations dwelt together; Minister of the Civil Service Li Shenjun often praised their family conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun, styled Bolü, was studious; three generations lived under one roof; Li Shenjun of the Ministry of Civil Service often praised their household.

sentences.zh: 位司徒諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He held the post of Consulting Aide to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was Consulting Aide to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 修起居注，拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: He compiled the Veritable Records and was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He edited the Veritable Records and was made Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部尚書、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of the Civil Service and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Minister of the Civil Service and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 恂弟惇。

translations.literal: Xun's younger brother Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's younger brother Dun.

sentences.zh: 惇字季良。

translations.literal: Dun was styled Jiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was styled Jiliang.

sentences.zh: 清識敏速，達于從政。

translations.literal: Clear in judgment and quick in perception, he excelled in administration.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-eyed and quick, he excelled at governing.

sentences.zh: 位司徒主簿，以明斷見知，時人號為「入鐵主簿」。

translations.literal: He was Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education and was known for clear decisions; men of the time called him "the iron-entering chief clerk."
translations.idiomatic: As Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education he was famed for decisive judgment; people called him "the iron-entering chief clerk."

sentences.zh: 稍遷陽平太守。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted Governor of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Governor of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 時遷都于鄴，陽平為畿郡，軍國責辦，賦斂無准。

translations.literal: At the time the capital was moved to Ye; Yangping was a metropolitan commandery; military and state requisitions were heavy and levies had no fixed measure.
translations.idiomatic: The court moved to Ye; Yangping was in the capital region; military levies were heavy and taxes had no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 又勳貴屬請，朝夕徵求。

translations.literal: Meritorious nobles' dependents also petitioned, demanding morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious nobles' kin also pressed demands day and night.

sentences.zh: 惇並禦之以道，咸以無怨，政為天下第一。

translations.literal: Dun with equal measure held them off by principle; all bore no resentment, and his government was ranked first under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Dun held them all to principle; none resented him, and his rule was ranked first in the realm.

sentences.zh: 特加賞異，圖形于闕，詔頒天下。

translations.literal: He received special reward and distinction; his likeness was painted at the palace gate and an edict circulated it through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He won special honors; his portrait was hung at the palace gate and an edict sent it through the empire.

sentences.zh: 曆魏尹、齊梁二州刺史，政並有治聲。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Intendant of Wei and Governor of the two provinces Qi and Liang; in each his administration had a reputation for good order.
translations.idiomatic: He was Intendant of Wei and Governor of Qi and Liang in turn; each post won him a name for good government.

sentences.zh: 遷大司農。

translations.literal: He was transferred Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 會王思政入據潁城，王師出討，惇常督軍，無乏絕。

translations.literal: When Wang Sizheng seized Yingcheng and the royal army went out against him, Dun regularly supervised the troops without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sizheng held Yingcheng and the royal army marched out, Dun kept the armies supplied without fail.

sentences.zh: 引洧水灌城，惇之策也。

translations.literal: Drawing the Wei River to flood the city was Dun's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Flooding the city by diverting the Wei was Dun's plan.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred Palace Attendant Within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Attendant Within the Hall.

sentences.zh: 惇美須，下垂至帶，省中號「長鬣公」。

translations.literal: Dun had handsome whiskers hanging down to his belt; within the ministry they called him "the Long-Whiskered Duke."
translations.idiomatic: Dun wore fine whiskers to his belt; colleagues called him "the Long-Whiskered Duke."

sentences.zh: 齊文宣嘗因酒酣，提惇須稱美；

translations.literal: Once when Qi Wenxuan was drunk he seized Dun's whiskers and praised their beauty;
translations.idiomatic: Once Wenxuan of Qi, drunk, seized Dun's beard and praised it;

sentences.zh: 以刀截之，唯留一握。

translations.literal: with a knife he cut them, leaving only a handful.
translations.idiomatic: then cut it with a knife, leaving only a fistful.

sentences.zh: 惇懼，因不復敢長，人又號「齊須公」。

translations.literal: Dun in fear thereafter dared not let them grow long again; people again called him "the Trim-Whiskered Duke."
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, Dun never let it grow long again; people then called him "the Trim-Whiskered Duke."

sentences.zh: 曆御史中丞、膠州刺史、司農大理二卿。

translations.literal: He held in succession Censor-in-Chief, Governor of Jiaozhou, and the two ministries of Agriculture and Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was Censor-in-Chief, Governor of Jiaozhou, and head of Agriculture and Justice in turn.

sentences.zh: 再為度支尚書、太子少保、少師、光祿大夫、開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射、特進，賜爵萬年縣子，食邑下邳郡幹。

translations.literal: Again he was Director of the Department of Revenue, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Junior Tutor, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, General-in-Chief with the authority of an office equal to the Three Dukes, Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, Special Advancement; he was granted the title Viscount of Wannian County with a fief of the dry fields of Xiapi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He again headed Revenue, served as Junior Guardian and Tutor, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, General-in-Chief with privilege equal to the Three Dukes, Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Special Advancement; he was made Viscount of Wannian with dry-field fief income from Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 惇年老，致仕於家。

translations.literal: Dun in old age retired to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Dun retired in old age.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he died.

sentences.zh: 惇少純直，晚更浮動。

translations.literal: Dun in youth was pure and upright; in later years he grew more restless.
translations.idiomatic: Young Dun was upright; in later years he grew opportunistic.

sentences.zh: 齊朝體式，本州大中正以京官為之。

translations.literal: Under Qi the provincial chief rectifier was by custom a capital official.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi the provincial chief rectifier was customarily a capital official.

sentences.zh: 乾明中，邢邵為中書監，德望甚高。

translations.literal: In the Qianming era Xing Shao was Director of the Secretariat; his virtue and standing were very high.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianming Xing Shao was Director of the Secretariat, famed for virtue.

sentences.zh: 惇與邵競中正。

translations.literal: Dun competed with Shao for the rectifier's post.
translations.idiomatic: Dun competed with Shao for chief rectifier.

sentences.zh: 遂憑附宋欽道，出邵為刺史，朝議甚鄙薄之。

translations.literal: He then relied on Song Qindao and had Shao sent out as governor; court opinion despised him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He leaned on Song Qindao and got Shao sent out as governor; the court despised him.

sentences.zh: 雖久處朝行，曆官清顯，與邢邵、魏收、陽休之、崔勵、徐之才比肩同列，諸人或談說經史，或吟詠詩賦，更相嘲戲，欣笑滿堂，惇不好劇談，又無學術，或坐杜口，或隱幾而睡，不為勝流所重。

translations.literal: Though long in the court ranks and holding clear, eminent offices, shoulder to shoulder with Xing Shao, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, Cui Li, and Xu Zhicai, some discoursed on the classics and histories, some chanted poetry and rhapsodies, mocking one another in turn with laughter filling the hall — Dun did not love lively talk and had no learning; sometimes he sat mute, sometimes he hid behind a armrest and slept — and was not esteemed by the leading men.
translations.idiomatic: Though he long held eminent posts beside Xing Shao, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, Cui Li, and Xu Zhicai — some debating classics, some reciting verse — Dun disliked banter and lacked learning; he sat silent or slept behind a screen and leading men did not respect him.

sentences.zh: 子文紀，武平末，度支郎中。

translations.literal: His son Wenji; at the end of Wuping he was a Director in the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenji was a Revenue Director at the end of Wuping.

sentences.zh: 文紀弟文經，勤學方雅，身無擇行，口無戲言。

translations.literal: Wenji's younger brother Wenjing studied diligently and was correct in manner; in person he chose no misconduct and in speech no jest.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Wenjing studied hard and lived correctly; he chose no bad conduct and spoke no idle words.

sentences.zh: 武平末，殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was Attendant Censor Within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was Attendant Censor Within the Hall.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，侍御史、兼通直散騎常侍、聘陳使副、主爵侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang era he was Attendant Censor, Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders Bearing the Direct Seal, deputy envoy on the mission to Chen, and Vice Minister of the Office of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaihuang he was Attendant Censor, concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, deputy envoy to Chen, and Vice Minister of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 卒于相州長史。

translations.literal: He died as Administrator of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Administrator of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 惇兄遜，字仲讓，有幹局。

translations.literal: Dun's elder brother Xun, styled Zhongrang, had administrative capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's elder brother Xun, styled Zhongrang, had real administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 乾明中，平原太守。

translations.literal: In the Qianming era he was Governor of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianming he was Governor of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈信州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Governor of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Governor of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 遜子文高，司徒掾。

translations.literal: Xun's son Wengao was a clerk to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's son Wengao was a clerk in the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 刁雍，字淑和，勃海饒安人也。

translations.literal: Diao Yong, styled Shuhe, was a man of Raoyan in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yong, styled Shuhe, came from Raoyan in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖協，從晉元帝度江，居京口，位尚書令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xie followed Jin Emperor Yuandi across the river, dwelt at Jingkou, and held the post of Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Xie followed Emperor Yuandi of Jin across the Yangtze, lived at Jingkou, and was Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 父暢，晉右衛將軍。

translations.literal: His father Chang was Right Guard General of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang was Right Guard General under Jin.

sentences.zh: 初，晉相劉裕微時，負社錢一萬，違時不還。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jin Chancellor Liu Yu was obscure, he owed ten thousand in community funds and failed to repay on time.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Chancellor Liu Yu of Jin was still obscure, he owed ten thousand in community funds and paid late.

sentences.zh: 暢兄逵執而征焉。

translations.literal: Chang's elder brother Kui seized and collected from him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's brother Kui seized him and demanded payment.

sentences.zh: 及誅桓玄，以嫌，先誅刁氏。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan was executed, because of enmity the Diao clan was first put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan was killed, the Diaos were executed first out of old grudge.

sentences.zh: 雍與暢故吏遂奔姚興，為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Yong and Chang's former clerks then fled to Yao Xing and became Junior Tutors to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Chang's old clerks fled to Yao Xing and became Junior Tutors to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 及姚泓滅，與司馬休之等歸魏，請于南境自效。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed, with Sima Xiuzhi and others he returned to Wei and asked to serve on the southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Hong fell, he returned to Wei with Sima Xiuzhi and others and offered service on the southern border.

sentences.zh: 明元假雍建威將軍。

translations.literal: Mingyuan provisionally made Yong General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan made him Acting General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 雍遂於河、濟間招集流散，傳檄邊境。

translations.literal: Yong then between the Yellow and Ji gathered the displaced and issued proclamations along the border.
translations.idiomatic: Yong gathered refugees between the Yellow and Ji and sent proclamations along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 雍弟彌，時亦率眾入京口，親共討裕。

translations.literal: Yong's younger brother Mi at the time also led troops into Jingkou to join in attacking Yu personally.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Mi also led men into Jingkou to attack Yu with him.

sentences.zh: 裕頻遣兵破之。

translations.literal: Yu repeatedly sent troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent troops repeatedly and broke them.

sentences.zh: 明元南幸鄴，雍朝於行宮。

translations.literal: Mingyuan on a southern tour came to Ye; Yong attended at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan toured south to Ye; Yong attended at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 明元問曰：「縛劉裕者，於卿親疏？

translations.literal: Mingyuan asked: "The one who would bind Liu Yu — to you is he near or far in kin?
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan asked: "The man who could bind Liu Yu — is he close kin to you?"

sentences.zh: 」雍曰：「伯父。

translations.literal: " Yong said: "My father's elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said: "My uncle."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「劉裕父子當應憚卿。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Liu Yu father and son ought to fear you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed: "Liu Yu and his son should fear you."

sentences.zh: 」於是假雍鎮東將軍、青州刺史、東光侯，使別立義軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yong was provisionally made General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of Qingzhou, and Marquis of Dongguang, and ordered to raise a separate loyal army.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was made Acting General Who Pacifies the East, Governor of Qingzhou, and Marquis of Dongguang, to raise a loyal force apart.

sentences.zh: 又詔雍令隨機立效。

translations.literal: An edict also told Yong to achieve merit as occasion offered.
translations.idiomatic: An edict told Yong to seize chances for merit.

sentences.zh: 雍於是招集譙、梁、彭、沛人五千餘家，置二十七營，遷鎮濟陰。

translations.literal: Yong then gathered more than five thousand households from Qiao, Liang, Peng, and Pei, established twenty-seven camps, and moved his headquarters to Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered five thousand-odd households from Qiao, Liang, Peng, and Pei, set twenty-seven camps, and moved to Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 遷徐州刺史，賜爵東安伯。

translations.literal: He was transferred Governor of Xuzhou and granted the title Earl of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He became Governor of Xuzhou and Earl of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 後除薄骨律鎮將。

translations.literal: Later he was made Garrison General of Bogulü.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Garrison General of Bogulü.

sentences.zh: 雍以西土乏雨，表求鑿渠，溉公私田。

translations.literal: Because the western lands lacked rain, Yong memorialized asking to dig canals to irrigate public and private fields.
translations.idiomatic: Rain failed in the west; Yong asked to dig canals for public and private fields.

sentences.zh: 又奉詔以高平、安定、統萬及薄骨律等四鎮，出車牛五千乘運屯谷五十萬斛付沃野，以供軍糧。

translations.literal: He also received an edict that from the four garrisons Gaoping, Anding, Tongwan, and Bogulü he should send five thousand cart-ox teams to transport five hundred thousand bushels of garrison grain to Woye to supply the armies.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he sent five thousand cart teams from four garrisons to move five hundred thousand bushels of grain to Woye for the armies.

sentences.zh: 道多深沙，車牛艱阻，求于牽屯山河水之次造船水運。

translations.literal: The road had much deep sand; carts and oxen were hard pressed; he asked to build boats at the Qiantun Mountain river for water transport.
translations.idiomatic: Deep sand blocked the road; he asked to build boats at Qiantun Mountain for river transport.

sentences.zh: 又以所綰邊表，常懼不虞，造城儲穀，置兵備守。

translations.literal: Also because the border he commanded was often in fear of surprise, he built a city, stored grain, and stationed troops to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing raids on his border, he built a city, stored grain, and posted guards.

sentences.zh: 詔皆從之。

translations.literal: Edicts approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved all.

sentences.zh: 詔即名此城為刁公城，以旌功焉。

translations.literal: The edict at once named this city Diao Duke's City, to display his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The city was named Duke Diao's City to honor his service.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，雍與隴西王源賀及中書監高允等並以耆年特見優禮，錫雍几杖，劍履上殿，月致珍羞焉。

translations.literal: In the Huangxing era Yong with Longxi's Wang Yuanhe and Director of the Secretariat Gao Yun and others were all aged and especially honored; Yong was granted a stool and staff, sword and shoes in the hall, and delicacies sent monthly.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangxing Yong with Wang Yuanhe of Longxi and Gao Yun, Director of the Secretariat, among other elders received special honor: stool and staff, sword and shoes in court, monthly delicacies.

sentences.zh: 雍性寬柔，好尚文典，手不釋書。

translations.literal: Yong by nature was gentle and broad, fond of literary canons; he never put down his books.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was gentle and loved literature; he never set books aside.

sentences.zh: 明敏多智，凡所為詩、賦、論、頌並諸雜文百有餘篇。

translations.literal: Clever and quick in wit, all the poems, rhapsodies, treatises, eulogies, and miscellaneous writings he made numbered more than a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted, he wrote more than a hundred poems, rhapsodies, essays, eulogies, and miscellany.

sentences.zh: 又泛施愛士，恬靜寡欲。

translations.literal: He also broadly showed love to scholars, was tranquil and had few desires.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous to scholars, tranquil, and little grasping.

sentences.zh: 篤信佛道，著《殺誡》二十餘篇以訓子孫。

translations.literal: He deeply believed in the Buddhist Way and wrote more than twenty chapters of Admonitions on Killing to instruct his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Devout in Buddhism, he wrote twenty-odd chapters of Admonitions on Killing for his heirs.

sentences.zh: 太和八年，卒，年九十五，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taihe he died at ninety-five; his posthumous title was Simple.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year eight he died at ninety-five; posthumous name Simple.

sentences.zh: 子遵。

translations.literal: His son Zun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zun.

sentences.zh: 遵字奉國，襲爵。

translations.literal: Zun was styled Fengguo and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Zun, styled Fengguo, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 遵少不拘小節，長更修改。

translations.literal: Zun in youth did not fuss over small points; grown, he amended himself further.
translations.idiomatic: Young Zun scorned small rules; grown, he reformed.

sentences.zh: 太和中，例降為侯。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, by precedent the rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe his rank was lowered by rule to marquis.

sentences.zh: 嘗經篤疾，幾死，見有神明救之，言福門子當享長年。

translations.literal: Once he suffered grave illness and nearly died; he saw a spirit save him, saying the son of Fujun would enjoy long years.
translations.idiomatic: Gravely ill, he nearly died; a spirit saved him, saying Fujun's son would live long.

sentences.zh: 後卒于洛州刺史，諡曰惠侯。

translations.literal: Later he died as Governor of Luozhou; posthumous title Marquis Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died Governor of Luozhou; posthumous title Marquis Hui.

sentences.zh: 子楷，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Kai died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kai died young.

sentences.zh: 楷子沖。

translations.literal: Kai's son Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's son Chong.

sentences.zh: 沖字文朗。

translations.literal: Chong was styled Wenlang.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was styled Wenlang.

sentences.zh: 十三而孤，孝慕過人。

translations.literal: Orphaned at thirteen, his filial longing surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at thirteen, his mourning devotion exceeded others'.

sentences.zh: 其祖母司空高允女，聰明婦人也。

translations.literal: His grandmother was the daughter of Minister of Works Gao Yun — a clever woman.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother was Gao Yun's daughter — a clever woman.

sentences.zh: 哀其早孤，撫養尤篤。

translations.literal: Pitying his early orphanhood, she reared him with especial tenderness.
translations.idiomatic: She pitied his early loss and reared him with special care.

sentences.zh: 沖免喪後，便志學他方，高氏泣涕留之，沖終不止。

translations.literal: After Chong left mourning he at once resolved to study elsewhere; the Gao clan wept and detained him, but Chong in the end did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he left to study abroad; the Gaos wept and begged him to stay, but he would not.

sentences.zh: 雖家世貴達，及從師於外，自同諸生。

translations.literal: Though his family was noble and eminent, when he followed teachers abroad he was the same as the other students.
translations.idiomatic: Though noble-born, abroad with his teachers he was like any student.

sentences.zh: 于時學制，諸生悉日直監廚。

translations.literal: At that time in the school system all students daily took turns supervising the kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Then every student took daily kitchen duty.

sentences.zh: 沖雖有僕隸，不令代己，身自炊爨。

translations.literal: Chong though he had servants did not let them replace him and cooked for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had servants Chong would not let them cook for him.

sentences.zh: 每師受之際，發志精專，不舍晝夜，殆忘寒暑。

translations.literal: Whenever he received instruction from a teacher he set his will with concentrated purpose, not resting day or night, nearly forgetting cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: Under a teacher he studied day and night, barely noting cold or heat.

sentences.zh: 學通諸經，偏修鄭說。

translations.literal: He mastered all the classics and especially cultivated the Zheng school.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics and favored the Zheng school.

sentences.zh: 陰陽、圖緯、算數、天文、風氣之書莫不關綜，當世服其精博。

translations.literal: Books on yin-yang, chart-weft texts, reckoning, astronomy, and wind-calendars — none he did not encompass; the age admired his depth and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Yin-yang, weft-charts, mathematics, astronomy, and wind lore — he mastered them all; contemporaries marveled at his range.

sentences.zh: 刺史郭祚聞其盛名，訪以疑義，沖應機解辯，無不祛其久惑。

translations.literal: Governor Guo Zuo heard his great fame and consulted him on doubtful points; Chong answered on the spot in debate and always dispelled their long-standing confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Guo Zuo sought him out on hard questions; Chong answered at once and cleared doubts held for years.

sentences.zh: 後太守范陽盧尚之、刺史河東裴桓並征沖為功曹主簿。

translations.literal: Later Governor Fanyang Lu Shangzhi and Governor Hedong Pei Huan both summoned Chong as Registrar Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Later Governors Lu Shangzhi of Fanyang and Pei Huan of Hedong both made him Registrar Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 非所好也，受署而已，不關事務，唯以講學為心。

translations.literal: Not his liking — he accepted appointment only and did not concern himself with affairs; his heart was solely in teaching.
translations.idiomatic: It was not his wish; he took title only, ignored office work, and gave his heart to lecturing.

sentences.zh: 四方學徒就其受業者，歲有數百。

translations.literal: Students from the four directions who came to study with him numbered hundreds each year.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of students came yearly from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 沖雖儒生，而執心壯烈，不畏強禦。

translations.literal: Though Chong was a Confucian scholar, his heart was fierce and he did not fear the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar by trade, Chong had a fierce heart and did not fear the mighty.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，帝舅司徒高肇擅恣威權，沖乃抗表極言其事。

translations.literal: In Yan Chang, the emperor's uncle Minister of Education Gao Zhao arrogantly grasped power; Chong submitted a memorial forcefully stating the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Yan Chang, the emperor's uncle Gao Zhao of the Ministry of Education abused power; Chong memorialized against him in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 辭旨懇直，文義忠憤，太傅、清河王懌覽而歎息。

translations.literal: The wording earnest and upright, the meaning loyal and angry — the Grand Tutor, Prince of Qinghe Hu, reading it, sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Earnest in tone, loyal and indignant in sense — Prince Hu of Qinghe, Grand Tutor, read it and sighed.

sentences.zh: 先是，沖曾祖雍作《行孝論》以誡子孫，稱古之葬者，衣之以薪，不封不樹。

translations.literal: Earlier Chong's great-grandfather Yong wrote "Treatise on Filial Conduct" to admonish descendants, saying ancient burials wrapped the body in brushwood, neither sealed nor tree-marked.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier great-grandfather Yong wrote a Treatise on Filial Conduct for his heirs, saying the ancients wrapped the dead in brushwood without mound or tree.

sentences.zh: 後世聖人，易之以棺槨。

translations.literal: Later sages replaced this with coffin and outer chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Later sages replaced that with coffin and outer chamber.

sentences.zh: 至秦以後，生則不能致養，死則厚葬過度。

translations.literal: From Qin onward, while alive they could not support their parents; dead, they over-buried extravagantly.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin, the living failed to support parents, yet the dead were buried with wasteful pomp.

sentences.zh: 及於末世，至蘧蒢裹屍，倮而葬者。

translations.literal: At the age's end some wrapped corpses in coarse grass mats and buried them naked.
translations.idiomatic: At the age's end some wrapped corpses in rush mats and buried them bare.

sentences.zh: 確而為論，並非折衷。

translations.literal: Those who held rigid theories were none of them the golden mean.
translations.idiomatic: Hard theorists on either side missed the mean.

sentences.zh: 既知二者之失，豈宜同之？

translations.literal: Knowing both extremes were wrong, how could one follow either?
translations.idiomatic: Knowing both were wrong, how follow either?

sentences.zh: 當令所存者，棺厚不過三寸，高不過三尺。

translations.literal: What should remain: coffin planks no thicker than three inches, height no more than three feet.
translations.idiomatic: What should remain: planks no thicker than three inches, height no more than three feet.

sentences.zh: 弗用繒采，斂以時服。

translations.literal: No silk brocade — shroud in timely dress.
translations.idiomatic: No brocade — only dress in season.

sentences.zh: 轜車止用白布為幔，不加畫飾，名為清素車。

translations.literal: The bier-carrying carriage uses only white cloth as canopy, without painted ornament — called the Plain-Simple Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral cart used only white cloth, unpainted — the Plain-Simple Carriage.

sentences.zh: 又去輓歌、方相並明器雜物。

translations.literal: Also remove dirge-songs, exorcist masks, and grave figurines and miscellany.
translations.idiomatic: Dirges, exorcist masks, and grave goods were also forbidden.

sentences.zh: 及沖祖遵將卒，敕其子孫，令奉雍遺旨。

translations.literal: When Chong's grandfather Zun was about to die, he charged descendants to follow Yong's testament.
translations.idiomatic: When grandfather Zun was dying, he ordered heirs to obey Yong's will.

sentences.zh: 河南尹丞張普惠謂為太儉，貽書于沖叔整。

translations.literal: Assistant of the Intendant of Henan Zhang Puhui called it too spare and sent a letter to Chong's uncle Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Puhui, assistant to the Intendant of Henan, called it too austere and wrote Chong's uncle Zheng.

sentences.zh: 令與通學議之。

translations.literal: He had them discuss it with fellow scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He asked fellow scholars to debate it.

sentences.zh: 沖乃致書國學諸儒，以論其事，學官竟不能答。

translations.literal: Chong then sent letters to the National University's Confucians to debate it; the academicians in the end could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Chong wrote the National University's scholars; none could refute him.

sentences.zh: 神抅末，沖以嫡傳祖爵東安侯。

translations.literal: At the end of Shengui, Chong by legitimate line inherited grandfather's title Marquis of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Shengui Chong inherited the Marquisate of Dong'an as legitimate heir.

sentences.zh: 京兆王繼為司空也，並以高選頻辟記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingzhao Ji was Minister of Works, he repeatedly by high selection summoned him as Recorder in the Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ji of Jingzhao was Minister of Works he repeatedly chose Chong as Recorder.

sentences.zh: 明帝將親釋奠，於是國子助教韓神固與諸儒詣國子祭酒崔光、吏部尚書甄琛，舉其才學，奏而征焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming was about to perform the libation-sacrifice in person; National University Assistant Tutor Han Shengu with the Confucians went to Rector Cui Guang and Minister of Civil Service Zhen Chen, commending his talent and learning; they memorialized and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming would sacrifice in person, Han Shengu and the scholars praised Chong to Cui Guang and Zhen Chen; he was summoned by memorial.

sentences.zh: 及卒，國子博士高涼及范陽盧道侃、盧景裕等復上狀陳沖業行，議奏諡曰安憲先生，祭乙太牢。

translations.literal: At his death, Academician Gao Liang of the National University and Fan yang's Lu Daokan and Lu Jingyu again submitted stating Chong's conduct; discussion fixed posthumous title Master Anxian, sacrifice with second-grade ox.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Gao Liang, Lu Daokan, and Lu Jingyu petitioned his merit; he received the posthumous title Master Anxian and a second-grade ox sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 子欽，字志儒，早亡。

translations.literal: His son Qin, styled Zhiru, died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qin, styled Zhiru, died young.

sentences.zh: 楷弟整，字景智。

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother Zheng, styled Jingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's younger brother Zheng, styled Jingzhi.

sentences.zh: 少有大度，頗涉書史。

translations.literal: In youth he had great breadth, having dipped into books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Young Zheng had large views and read widely in history.

sentences.zh: 太和十五年，為奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe he was a court gentleman in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year fifteen he was a court gentleman in attendance.

sentences.zh: 孝文都洛，親自臨選，除司空法曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang and personally supervised selection, he was made Law Bureau Attendant of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen moved to Luoyang and chose officials himself, Zheng became Law Bureau Attendant under the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 累遷黃門郎。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，假征東大將軍、滄冀瀛三州刺史、大都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was Acting General Who Conquers the East, Governor of the three provinces Cang, Ji, and Ying, and Great Governor.
translations.idiomatic: At Putai's start he was Acting General Who Conquers the East, Governor of Cang, Ji, and Ying, and Great Governor.

sentences.zh: 尋加車騎將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon added General of Cavalry and Grand Master with the Splendor of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he added General of Cavalry and Grand Master with the Splendor of the Right.

sentences.zh: 遂逢本鄉賊亂，奉母客于齊州。

translations.literal: He then met chaos from bandits in his home region and took his mother as guest to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit chaos in his homeland drove him to shelter his mother in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 既而母卒。

translations.literal: Soon after his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his mother died.

sentences.zh: 母即高允之女。

translations.literal: His mother was the daughter of Gao Yun.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Gao Yun's daughter.

sentences.zh: 崔光、崔亮皆經允接待，是以涼燠之際，光等每致拜焉。

translations.literal: Cui Guang and Cui Liang had both been received by Yun — therefore in moments of ceremony Guang and others would pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang and Cui Liang had been fostered by Yun; at ritual moments they still bowed to the widow.

sentences.zh: 天平四年，卒於鄴，贈司空公，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping he died at Ye; posthumously Minister of Works, posthumous title Literary Offering.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year four he died at Ye; posthumously Minister of Works, posthumous name Literary Offering.

sentences.zh: 整解音律，輕財好施，交結名勝，聲酒自娛。

translations.literal: Zheng understood pitch and mode, was light with wealth and generous, bonded with celebrated men, amused himself with sound and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng knew music, spent freely, courted famous men, and lived by wine and song.

sentences.zh: 然貪而好色，為議者所貶。

translations.literal: Yet he was greedy and fond of women — censured by critics.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy and lustful — critics despised him.

sentences.zh: 子柔。

translations.literal: His son Rou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rou.

sentences.zh: 柔字子溫。

translations.literal: Rou was styled Ziwen.
translations.idiomatic: Rou was styled Ziwen.

sentences.zh: 少好學，留心儀禮，性強記，至於氏族內外，皆所諳悉。

translations.literal: He loved learning young, attentive to ritual; his memory was strong — inner and outer of the clans he knew thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: He studied young, minded ritual, and remembered every kin near and far.

sentences.zh: 居母喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Mourning his mother he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His mourning for his mother won fame for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 初為魏宣武挽郎，解巾司空行參軍。

translations.literal: At first he was a dirge-officer for Emperor Xuanwu of Wei, then donned cap as Attendant in the Ministry of Works' Office.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a dirge-officer for Emperor Xuanwu of Wei, then became an Attendant in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，累遷國子博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao he rose through posts to Doctor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi Tianbao's start he rose to Doctor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 中書令魏收撰魏史，啟柔等同其事。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Wei Shou compiled the History of Wei and had Rou and others join the work.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, Director of the Secretariat, drafting the History of Wei, enlisted Rou and others.

sentences.zh: 柔性專固，自是所聞，收常嫌憚。

translations.literal: Rou's nature was obstinate; on what he had heard himself Shou often feared and held back.
translations.idiomatic: Rou was stubborn; on matters he knew firsthand Shou often held back in fear.

sentences.zh: 又參議律令。

translations.literal: He also took part in deliberating statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped draft statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 時議者以為五等爵邑承襲，無嫡子，立嫡孫；

translations.literal: Critics then held that in succession of five-rank enfeoffments: without legitimate son, establish legitimate grandson;
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that for five-rank fiefs: without a legitimate son, name a legitimate grandson;

sentences.zh: 無嫡孫，立嫡子弟；

translations.literal: without legitimate grandson, establish legitimate younger brother's son;
translations.idiomatic: without a legitimate grandson, name the legitimate younger brother's son;

sentences.zh: 園嫡子弟，立嫡孫弟。

translations.literal: without legitimate younger brother's son, establish legitimate grandson's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: without that, name the legitimate grandson's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 柔以為無嫡孫，應立嫡曾孫，不應立嫡子弟。

translations.literal: Rou held that without legitimate grandson one should establish legitimate great-grandson, not legitimate younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Rou argued that without a legitimate grandson one should name a legitimate great-grandson, not the younger brother's son.

sentences.zh: 議曰：

translations.literal: The discussion says:
translations.idiomatic: The discussion runs:

sentences.zh: 案《禮》，立嫡以長，故謂長子為嫡子。

translations.literal: Examining the Rites: establishment of heir is by seniority, hence the eldest son is called legitimate son.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say the heir is the eldest; hence the eldest son is the legitimate son.

sentences.zh: 嫡子死，以嫡子之子為嫡孫，死則曾、玄亦然。

translations.literal: When the legitimate son dies, the legitimate son's son is legitimate grandson; when he dies, great-great likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When the legitimate son dies, his son is legitimate grandson; the same through great-great-grandsons.

sentences.zh: 然則嫡子之名本為傳重。

translations.literal: Thus the name legitimate son was originally for transmitting the heavy obligation.
translations.idiomatic: So the name "legitimate son" exists to carry the ancestral burden.

sentences.zh: 故《喪服》曰：「庶子不為長子三年，不繼祖與禰也。

translations.literal: Hence the Mourning Garments says: "A secondary son does not observe three years for the eldest son — he does not continue grandfather and father."
translations.idiomatic: Mourning Garments says: "A secondary son does not mourn the eldest three years — he does not continue grandfather and father."

sentences.zh: 」《禮》：「公儀仲子之喪，檀弓曰：'我未之前聞也。

translations.literal: The Rites: "At the mourning for Zhongzi of Gongyi, Tan Gong said: 'I have not heard of this before.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites record: at Zhongzi of Gongyi's mourning Tan Gong said, "I have never heard of this.

sentences.zh: 仲子舍其孫而立其子，何也？

translations.literal: Zhongzi abandoned his grandson and established his son — why?'
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzi set aside his grandson for his son — why?"

sentences.zh: '子服伯子曰：'仲子亦猶行古之道也。

translations.literal: Zifu Bo said: 'Zhongzi also followed the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: Zifu Bo said, "Zhongzi followed ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 昔者文王舍伯邑考而立武王發，微子舍其孫腯而立其弟衍。

translations.literal: Formerly King Wen abandoned Bo Yikao and established King Wu Fa; Weizi abandoned his grandson Tun and established his younger brother Yan.'"
translations.idiomatic: King Wen set aside Bo Yikao for King Wu Fa; Weizi set aside grandson Tun for younger brother Yan."

sentences.zh: '」鄭注曰：「仲子為親者諱耳，立子非也。

translations.literal: Zheng's note says: 'Zhongzi was covering for kin — establishing the son was not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng comments: Zhongzi was sparing kin's shame — naming the son was wrong.

sentences.zh: 文王之立武王，權也。

translations.literal: King Wen establishing King Wu was expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Wen naming Wu was expedient.

sentences.zh: 微子嫡子死，立弟衍，殷禮也。

translations.literal: Weizi's legitimate son died — establishing younger brother Yan was Yin rite.'"
translations.idiomatic: Weizi's legitimate son died; naming Yan followed Yin rite."

sentences.zh: 」「子游問諸孔子，孔子曰：'不，立孫。

translations.literal: "Ziyou asked Confucius; Confucius said: 'No — establish the grandson.'"
translations.idiomatic: Ziyou asked Confucius; Confucius said, "No — establish the grandson."

sentences.zh: '」注商以嫡子死，立嫡子之母弟；

translations.literal: Notes: Yin when legitimate son dies establishes legitimate son's mother-younger-brother;
translations.idiomatic: Commentators: Yin, when the legitimate son dies, names the mother's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 周以嫡子死，立嫡子之子為嫡孫。

translations.literal: Zhou when legitimate son dies establishes legitimate son's son as legitimate grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou names the legitimate son's son as legitimate grandson.

sentences.zh: 故《春秋公羊》之義，嫡子有孫而死，質家親親先立弟，文家尊尊先立孫。

translations.literal: Thus the meaning of Spring and Autumn Gongyang: if legitimate son has a grandson who dies, the plain school by cherishing kin first establishes the younger brother; the cultured school by honoring honor first establishes the grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyang's Spring and Autumn: if the legitimate son leaves a grandson who dies, the plain school favors kin and names the younger brother first; the cultured school favors rank and names the grandson first.

sentences.zh: 《喪服》云：「為父後者，為出母無服。

translations.literal: Mourning Garments says: "One who is heir to the father wears no mourning for the divorced mother."
translations.idiomatic: Mourning Garments: "He who continues the father wears no mourning for a divorced mother."

sentences.zh: 」《小記》云：「祖父卒而後為祖母後者，三年。

translations.literal: Lesser Record says: "One who after grandfather's death becomes heir to grandmother — three years."
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Record: "He who after grandfather's death becomes grandmother's heir — three years."

sentences.zh: 」為母無服者，不祭故也。

translations.literal: No mourning for mother — because he does not sacrifice to her.
translations.idiomatic: No mourning for mother — he does not sacrifice to her.

sentences.zh: 為祖母三年者，大宗傳重故也。

translations.literal: Three years for grandmother — because the great lineage transmits the heavy obligation.
translations.idiomatic: Three years for grandmother — the great line still carries the burden.

sentences.zh: 今議以嫡孫死而立嫡子母弟。

translations.literal: Now the discussion holds: when legitimate grandson dies, establish legitimate son's mother-younger-brother.
translations.idiomatic: The present view: when the legitimate grandson dies, name the legitimate son's mother's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 嫡子母弟者，則為父後矣。

translations.literal: The legitimate son's mother-younger-brother is then heir to the father.
translations.idiomatic: That younger brother would then continue the father.

sentences.zh: 嫡子母弟本非承嫡，以無嫡，故得為父後，則嫡孫之弟，理亦應得為父後，則是父卒然後為祖後者服斬。

translations.literal: The legitimate son's mother-younger-brother by nature does not inherit the legitimate line — because there is no legitimate heir he may become heir to the father; then the legitimate grandson's younger brother by reason should also be able to become heir to the father — that is wearing the finest mourning for becoming grandfather's heir after father's death.
translations.idiomatic: That brother is not born to the legitimate line; only for lack of heir may he continue the father — then the legitimate grandson's younger brother should equally continue the father, which means finest mourning as grandfather's heir after the father dies.

sentences.zh: 既得為祖服斬，而不得為傳重，未之聞也。

translations.literal: If one may wear finest mourning for grandfather yet may not transmit the heavy obligation — unheard of.
translations.idiomatic: To wear grandfather's finest mourning yet not carry the burden — unheard of.

sentences.zh: 若用商家親親之義，本不應舍嫡子而立嫡孫。

translations.literal: If using Yin merchants' meaning of cherishing kin, one should not abandon legitimate son to establish legitimate grandson.
translations.idiomatic: By Yin's kin-first rule one should not pass the legitimate son for the grandson.

sentences.zh: 若從周家尊尊之文，豈宜舍其孫而立其弟？

translations.literal: If following Zhou's text of honoring honor, how can one abandon the grandson and establish the younger brother?
translations.idiomatic: By Zhou's honor-first rule how abandon the grandson for the younger brother?

sentences.zh: 或文或質，愚用或焉。

translations.literal: Whether cultured or plain — a fool uses whichever suits.
translations.idiomatic: Cultured or plain — a fool picks whichever helps his case.

sentences.zh: 《小記》云：「嫡婦為舅姑後者，則舅姑為之小功。

translations.literal: Lesser Record says: "When the legitimate wife becomes heir to parents-in-law, then parents-in-law wear for her lesser service."
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Record: "When the legitimate wife becomes heir to her in-laws, they wear lesser mourning for her."

sentences.zh: 」注云：「謂夫有廢疾、他故，若死無子，不受重者。

translations.literal: Note: It means if the husband has disabling illness or other cause, or dies without son and does not receive the heavy obligation.
translations.idiomatic: The note: if the husband is crippled or otherwise cannot receive the burden, or dies without a son.

sentences.zh: 小功，庶婦之服。

translations.literal: Lesser service is secondary wife's garb.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser service is a concubine's mourning.

sentences.zh: 凡父母于子，舅姑于婦，將不傳重於嫡，及將所傳重者非嫡，服之皆如眾子庶婦也。

translations.literal: Generally parents to sons, parents-in-law to wives — when about to transmit the heavy obligation to one who is not legitimate, or when the one to receive the heavy obligation is not legitimate, the garb is all like common sons and secondary wives.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever parents or in-laws will not pass the burden to a legitimate heir, or the receiver is not legitimate, mourning matches that for ordinary sons and concubines.

sentences.zh: 」言死無子者，謂絕世。

translations.literal: "Dies without son" means the line ends.
translations.idiomatic: "Dies without son" means the line ends.

sentences.zh: 無子，非謂無嫡子。

translations.literal: Without son does not mean without legitimate son.
translations.idiomatic: It does not mean without a legitimate son.

sentences.zh: 如其子，焉得雲無後？

translations.literal: If there were his son, how say without posterity?
translations.idiomatic: If there is a son, how call it without posterity?

sentences.zh: 夫雖廢疾無子，婦猶以嫡為名。

translations.literal: Though the husband be disabled without son, the wife still bears the name legitimate.
translations.idiomatic: Though the husband be crippled and sonless, the wife is still called legitimate.

sentences.zh: 嫡名既在，而欲廢其子者如禮何？

translations.literal: The name legitimate being present, yet wishing to displace her son — how by the rites?
translations.idiomatic: With the name legitimate still in place, displacing her son — how by ritual?

sentences.zh: 禮何有損益，革代相沿。

translations.literal: How can rites have increase and decrease, dynasty replacing dynasty in succession?
translations.idiomatic: Rites may wax and wane, yet dynasties follow one another — can the lineage heir change at will?

sentences.zh: 必謂宗嫡可得而變者，則為後服斬亦宜有因而改。

translations.literal: If one must say the lineage heir can be changed, then finest mourning as heir should also be changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: If the heir may be swapped, finest mourning as heir should swap with him.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he died.

sentences.zh: 柔在史館未久，勒成之際，志在偏黨。

translations.literal: Rou had not long been in the History Office; at the moment of compilation his aim was partisan.
translations.idiomatic: Rou had not long been in the History Office; at compilation he favored his kin.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》中與其內外通親者，並虛美過實，為時論所譏。

translations.literal: Kin inside and outside in the History of Wei — all were praised beyond fact; critics of the time mocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Kin inside and outside in the History of Wei were flattered beyond truth — contemporaries mocked it.

sentences.zh: 整弟宣，字季達。

translations.literal: Zheng's younger brother Xuan, styled Jida.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's younger brother Xuan, styled Jida.

sentences.zh: 以功封高城縣侯，歷位都官尚書、衛大將軍、滄州刺史。

translations.literal: By merit enfeoffed Marquis of Gaocheng; held in succession Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Guardian General, Governor of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By merit he was Marquis of Gaocheng; he headed the Imperial Clan Court, served as Guardian General, and governed Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉公，諡曰武。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously Grand Preceptor, posthumous title Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously Grand Preceptor, posthumous name Martial.

sentences.zh: 刁氏世有榮貴，而門風不甚修潔，為時所鄙。

translations.literal: The Diao clan for generations had glory, yet household conduct was not very clean — despised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Diaos were long eminent, yet their household manners were coarse — the age despised them.

sentences.zh: 雍族孫雙，字子山。

translations.literal: Yong's clan grandson Shuang, styled Zishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's clansman Shuang, styled Zishan.

sentences.zh: 高祖藪，晉齊郡太守。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Sou was Governor of Qi commandery under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Great-great-grandfather Sou was Jin's Governor of Qi commandery.

sentences.zh: 藪因晉亂，居青州之安樂。

translations.literal: Because of Jin's turmoil Sou dwelt at Anle in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin fell into chaos Sou settled at Anle in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 至雙始歸本鄉。

translations.literal: Only when Shuang came did he return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was the first to return home.

sentences.zh: 雙少好學，兼涉文史，雅為中山王英所知賞。

translations.literal: Shuang in youth loved learning and also dipped into literature and history; he was elegantly known and prized by Prince of Zhongshan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Young Shuang loved books and history; Prince Ying of Zhongshan prized him.

sentences.zh: 位西河太守。

translations.literal: He held the post of Governor of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: He became Governor of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 為政清簡，吏人安悅。

translations.literal: His government was clear and simple; officials and people were at ease and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled plainly; officials and people were content.

sentences.zh: 及中山王熙起兵誅元叉，事敗，熙弟略投命於雙。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhongshan Xi raised troops to execute Yuan Cha and failed, Xi's younger brother Lüe threw himself on Shuang's mercy.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xi of Zhongshan rose against Yuan Cha and failed, his brother Lüe sought refuge with Shuang.

sentences.zh: 雙藏護周年。

translations.literal: Shuang hid and protected him a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang hid him for a full year.

sentences.zh: 時購略甚切，略懼，求送出境。

translations.literal: At the time the price on Lüe's head was very keen; Lüe in fear asked to be sent beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Bounty hunters pressed hard; Lüe begged to be sent abroad.

sentences.zh: 雙曰：「會有一死，所難過耳。

translations.literal: Shuang said: "There will be one death — that alone is hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang said, "Death comes once — that is the hard part.

sentences.zh: 今遭知己，視死如歸，願不以為慮。

translations.literal: Now meeting a true friend, I view death as returning home — please do not worry on my account.
translations.idiomatic: Now I meet a true friend and welcome death as homecoming — do not fret for me."

sentences.zh: 」略復苦求南轉，雙乃遣從子昌送達江左。

translations.literal: Lüe again pressed hard to turn south; Shuang then sent his nephew Chang to escort him to the lands east of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Lüe still begged to go south; Shuang sent nephew Chang to deliver him to the south.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，知略因雙獲濟，徵拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored the government, learning Lüe had been saved through Shuang, she summoned and appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power she learned Lüe owed his escape to Shuang and made Lüe Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時略姊饒安主，刁宣妻也，頻訴靈太后，乞征略還。

translations.literal: At the time Lüe's elder sister was Princess Rao'an, wife of Diao Xuan; she repeatedly appealed to Empress Dowager Ling, begging to summon Lüe back.
translations.idiomatic: Lüe's sister, Princess Rao'an, wife of Diao Xuan, repeatedly begged the empress dowager to recall him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷乃以徐州所獲俘江革、祖暼恆二人易之。

translations.literal: The court then exchanged him for the two captives taken at Xuzhou, Jiang Ge and Zu Yunheng.
translations.idiomatic: The court traded him for two captives from Xuzhou — Jiang Ge and Zu Yunheng.

sentences.zh: 以雙與略有舊，乃令至境迎接。

translations.literal: Because Shuang and Lüe were old friends, he was ordered to the border to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: As Shuang and Lüe were old friends, Shuang was sent to the frontier to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 明帝末，除西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Ming's reign he was made Governor of Western Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Ming's reign he became Governor of Western Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時賊盜蜂起，州人張桃弓等招聚亡命，公行劫掠。

translations.literal: At the time bandits swarmed; men of the province Zhang Taogong and others gathered fugitives and openly plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed; Zhang Taogong and others rallied outlaws and robbed openly.

sentences.zh: 雙至境，先遣使諭桃弓，陳示禍福，桃弓即隨使歸罪，雙舍而不問。

translations.literal: Shuang on reaching the border first sent envoys to instruct Taogong, setting forth fortune and ruin; Taogong at once followed the envoy to confess guilt, and Shuang released him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: At the border Shuang sent envoys to Taogong with warning of consequences; Taogong surrendered at once and Shuang pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 後有盜發之處，令桃弓追捕，咸悉禽獲，於是州境清肅。

translations.literal: Later wherever robbers struck he had Taogong pursue them; all were captured — and the province grew orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Later he set Taogong to hunt every robbery; all were caught and the province grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，行濟州刺史，以功封曲城鄉男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he acted as Governor of Jizhou and by merit was enfeoffed Baron of Qucheng township.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaozhuang's start he acted as Governor of Jizhou and was made Baron of Qucheng.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，遷驍騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was transferred General of Valiant Cavalry and Grand Master with the Splendor of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaowu's start he became General of Valiant Cavalry and Grand Master with the Splendor of the Left.

sentences.zh: 興和三年，卒，贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、齊州刺史，諡曰清穆。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xinghe he died; posthumously General of Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Governor of Qizhou, posthumous title Clear and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe year three he died; posthumously General of Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Governor of Qizhou, posthumous name Clear and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 辛紹先，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Xin Shaoxian was a man of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Shaoxian came from Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 五世祖怡，晉幽州刺史。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Yi was Governor of Youzhou under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-generation ancestor Yi was Jin's Governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 父深，仕西涼為驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: His father Shen served Western Liang as General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen was General of Valiant Cavalry under Western Liang.

sentences.zh: 及涼後主歆與沮渠蒙遜戰於蓼泉，軍敗，失馬，深以所乘授歆，而身死於難。

translations.literal: When Liang's last ruler Xin fought Zuju Mengxun at Liaooquan the army was defeated; Xin lost his horse; Shen gave the mount he rode to Xin and himself died in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When the last Liang ruler Xin fought Mengxun at Liaooquan and lost his horse, Shen gave him his mount and died in the rout.

sentences.zh: 以義烈見稱西土。

translations.literal: For righteous valor he was famed in the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: His sacrifice won fame in the west.

sentences.zh: 涼州平，紹先內徙，家于晉陽。

translations.literal: When Liangzhou was pacified Shaoxian moved inward and made his home at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzhou fell Shaoxian moved inland to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 明敏有識量，與廣平遊明根、范陽盧度世、同郡李承昭等甚相友。

translations.literal: Clever and perceptive with judgment, he was very friendly with Guangping's You Minggen, Fanyang's Lu Dushi, and his fellow commandery-man Li Chengshao.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and discerning, he befriended You Minggen of Guangping, Lu Dushi of Fanyang, and Li Chengshao of his commandery.

sentences.zh: 有至性，丁父憂，三年口不甘味，頭不櫛沐，發遂落盡，故常著垂裙皁帽。

translations.literal: He had utmost nature; in mourning his father for three years his mouth knew no savor and his head knew no combing — his hair fell out entirely, so he always wore a long-skirted black cap.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly filial, he mourned his father three years without tasting food or combing hair until it fell out; he wore a long black mourning cap thereafter.

sentences.zh: 自中書博士轉神部令。

translations.literal: From Doctor of the Palace Secretariat he was transferred Director of the Spirit Department.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Doctor of the Palace Secretariat to Director of the Spirit Department.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，薛安都以彭城歸魏。

translations.literal: In Huangxing Xue Anyi surrendered Pengcheng to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangxing Xue Anyi surrendered Pengcheng to Wei.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷欲綏安初附，以紹先為下邳太守。

translations.literal: The court then wished to soothe the newly attached; Shaoxian was made Governor of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: The court wished to soothe new subjects and made Shaoxian Governor of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 為政不甚皦察，舉其不綱而已，唯教人為產禦賊之備。

translations.literal: His government was not very scrutinizing — he raised only what was out of line and otherwise taught people to build livelihood and prepare against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled lightly, correcting only gross abuses and teaching people to prosper and guard against raiders.

sentences.zh: 及宋將陳顯達、蕭道成、蕭順之來寇，道成謂順之曰：「辛紹先未易侵也，宜共慎之。

translations.literal: When Song generals Chen Xianda, Xiao Daocheng, and Xiao Shunzhi came to raid, Daocheng told Shunzhi: "Xin Shaoxian is not easy to invade — we should together be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: When Song's Chen Xianda, Xiao Daocheng, and Xiao Shunzhi raided, Daocheng told Shunzhi, "Xin Shaoxian is not easy prey — be careful together."

sentences.zh: 」於是不曆郡境，徑屯呂梁。

translations.literal: " Therefore they did not cross the commandery border but camped straight at Lüliang.
translations.idiomatic: They did not enter the commandery but camped at Lüliang.

sentences.zh: 卒於郡，贈并州刺史、晉陽侯，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: He died in the commandery; posthumously Governor of Bingzhou and Marquis of Jinyang, posthumous title Kind.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; posthumously Governor of Bingzhou and Marquis of Jinyang, posthumous name Kind.

sentences.zh: 子鳳達，耽道樂古，有長者之名。

translations.literal: His son Fengda loved the Way and delighted in antiquity; he had the name of an elder.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengda loved the Way and antiquity and was called a man of stature.

sentences.zh: 卒于京兆王子推國常侍。

translations.literal: He died as Regular Attendant in the state of Prince of Jingzhao Zitui.
translations.idiomatic: He died Regular Attendant to Prince Zitui of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 鳳達子祥，字萬福。

translations.literal: Fengda's son Xiang, styled Wanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Fengda's son Xiang, styled Wanfu.

sentences.zh: 舉司州秀才，再遷司空主簿。

translations.literal: Recommended as Xiuzhou provincial graduate, twice promoted to Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: A Xiuzhou graduate, he twice rose to Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧妃，即祥妻之妹也。

translations.literal: The consort of Prince of Xianyang Xi was the younger sister of Xiang's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang's consort was sister to Xiang's wife.

sentences.zh: 及禧構逆，親知多罹塵謗，詳獨蕭然不預。

translations.literal: When Xi plotted rebellion, kin and friends mostly fell into slander; Xiang alone stood apart and took no part.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi rebelled, kin and friends were ruined; Xiang alone kept clear.

sentences.zh: 轉并州平北府司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred Military Secretary of the Pingbei Headquarters in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became Military Secretary of Bingzhou's Pingbei Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 有白壁還兵藥道顯，被誣為賊，官屬咸疑之。

translations.literal: A returned soldier from Baibi named Yao Daoxian was accused as a bandit; all officials suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: A Baibi soldier, Yao Daoxian, was accused of banditry; officials doubted him.

sentences.zh: 詳曰：「道顯面有悲色。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Daoxian's face bears grief.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Daoxian's face shows grief.

sentences.zh: 察獄以色，其此之謂乎！

translations.literal: To judge a prison case by complexion — is this not that saying?"
translations.idiomatic: To read guilt in the face — is this not that very thing?"

sentences.zh: 」苦執申之。

translations.literal: He firmly insisted on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed hard for him.

sentences.zh: 月餘，別獲真賊。

translations.literal: After more than a month the real bandits were captured elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: A month later the real bandits were caught elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 後除郢州龍驤府長史，帶義陽太守。

translations.literal: Later he was made Longma Headquarters Secretary in Yingzhou, concurrently Governor of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Longma Headquarters Secretary in Yingzhou, concurrently Governor of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 白早生之反也，梁遣來援，因此緣淮鎮戍，相繼降沒。

translations.literal: When Bai Zaosheng rebelled Liang sent aid; because of this garrisons along the Huai surrendered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Zaosheng rebelled Liang sent help; Huai garrisons fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 唯祥堅城固守。

translations.literal: Only Xiang held the city firm.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xiang held firm.

sentences.zh: 梁又遣將胡武城、陶平虜，于州南金山之上，連營侵逼。

translations.literal: Liang also sent generals Hu Wucheng and Tao Pinglu; on Golden Mountain south of the province they linked camps and pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Hu Wucheng and Tao Pinglu to camp on Golden Mountain south of the province and press the siege.

sentences.zh: 祥出其不意，襲之。

translations.literal: Xiang struck where they did not expect.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang struck unexpectedly.

sentences.zh: 賊大崩，禽平虜，斬武城，以送京師。

translations.literal: The bandits collapsed greatly; he captured Pinglu, beheaded Wucheng, and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke; he seized Pinglu, beheaded Wucheng, and sent heads to court.

sentences.zh: 州境獲全。

translations.literal: The province was wholly preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The province was saved entire.

sentences.zh: 論功方有賞授，而刺史婁悅恥勳出其下，間之執政，事竟不行。

translations.literal: Merit was about to be rewarded when Governor Lou Yue, shamed that the achievement ranked below his, spoke against it to the administration — in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were due when Governor Lou Yue, ashamed the glory outshone him, slandered him at court — nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 胡賊劉龍駒作逆華州，除祥安定王燮征虜府長史，仍為別將，與討胡使薛和滅之。

translations.literal: When Hu bandit Liu Longju rebelled in Huazhou, Xiang was made Military Secretary of Prince of Anding Xie's Pacification Headquarters and also Separate Commander; with the Hu-pacification envoy Xue He he destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Longju rebelled in Huazhou, Xiang served Prince Xie of Anding as Military Secretary and Separate Commander and with Xue He destroyed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈南青州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously Governor of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously Governor of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祥弟少雍，字季和，少聰穎，有孝行，尤為祖父紹先所愛。

translations.literal: Xiang's younger brother Shaoyong, styled Jihe, was clever in youth, filial in conduct, and especially loved by grandfather Shaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Shaoyong, styled Jihe, was bright and filial and especially loved by grandfather Shaoxian.

sentences.zh: 紹先性嗜羊肝，常呼少雍共食。

translations.literal: Shaoxian by nature loved sheep liver and often called Shaoyong to eat with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxian loved sheep liver and often shared it with Shaoyong.

sentences.zh: 及紹先卒，少雍終身不食肝。

translations.literal: When Shaoxian died Shaoyong never ate liver all his life.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaoxian died Shaoyong never touched liver again.

sentences.zh: 性仁厚，有禮義，門內之法，為時所重。

translations.literal: By nature humane and thick, with ritual propriety — household law within the gates was weighty in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Humane and courteous, his household rules were famed.

sentences.zh: 稍遷司空、高陽王雍田曹參軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted Field Bureau Attendant under the Ministry of Works and Prince of Gaoyang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Field Bureau Attendant under the Ministry of Works and Prince Yong of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 少雍清正，不憚強禦，積年久訟，造次決之。

translations.literal: Shaoyong was upright and clear, not fearing the powerful; lawsuits piled for years — he decided them on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and fearless, he ended lawsuits years old in a single sitting.

sentences.zh: 請托路絕，時稱賢明。

translations.literal: The path of patronage was cut off; the age called him wise and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Favor-seekers found no door; men called him wise.

sentences.zh: 正始中，詔百官各舉所知，高陽王雍及吏部郎中李憲俱以少雍為舉首。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi an edict had every office recommend those it knew; Prince Yong of Gaoyang and Personnel Director Li Xian both put Shaoyong first.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi each office was to recommend talent; Prince Yong and Li Xian of Personnel both named Shaoyong first.

sentences.zh: 卒於給事中。

translations.literal: He died as Supervisor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He died Supervisor in the Palace.

sentences.zh: 少雍妻王氏，有德義。

translations.literal: Shaoyong's wife the Wang clan had virtue and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His wife of the Wang clan had virtue.

sentences.zh: 少雍與從弟懷仁兄弟同居。

translations.literal: Shaoyong and his cousin Huairen's brothers dwelt together.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyong lived with cousin Huairen's household.

sentences.zh: 懷仁等事之甚謹，閨門禮讓，人無間焉。

translations.literal: Huairen and the others served him very respectfully; ritual courtesy within the women's quarters — no one found fault.
translations.idiomatic: Huairen's family served him scrupulously; no one faulted their courtesy.

sentences.zh: 士大夫以此稱美。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials for this praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars praised them for it.

sentences.zh: 子元桓，武定中，儀同府司馬。

translations.literal: His son Yuanhuan; in Wuding era, Military Secretary of the Equal-in-Honor Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanhuan was Military Secretary of an Equal-in-Honor Headquarters in Wuding.

sentences.zh: 元桓弟遜士，太師開府功曹參軍。

translations.literal: Yuanhuan's younger brother Xunshi was Administrative Clerk in the Grand Preceptor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Xunshi was clerk in the Grand Preceptor's office.

sentences.zh: 鳳達弟穆，字叔宗，舉茂才，東雍州別駕。

translations.literal: Fengda's younger brother Mu, styled Shuzong, was recommended as Maocai and became Aide of Eastern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fengda's younger brother Mu, styled Shuzong, was a Maocai graduate and Aide of Eastern Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 初隨父在下邳，與彭城陳敬文友善。

translations.literal: At first he followed his father in Xiapi and was friendly with Pengcheng's Chen Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed his father to Xiapi and befriended Chen Jingwen of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 敬文弟敬武，少為沙門，從師遠學，經久不返。

translations.literal: Jingwen's younger brother Jingwu in youth became a monk, followed teachers far to study, and long did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Jingwu became a monk and studied abroad for years without return.

sentences.zh: 敬文病臨卒，以雜綾二十匹托穆與敬武。

translations.literal: Jingwen, ill and near death, entrusted twenty bolts of mixed silk to Mu for Jingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, Jingwen entrusted twenty bolts of silk to Mu for Jingwu.

sentences.zh: 穆久不得見，經二十年，始於洛陽見敬武，以物還之，封題如故。

translations.literal: Mu long could not see him; after twenty years he met Jingwu in Luoyang and returned the goods — the seal and inscription as before.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years later Mu met Jingwu in Luoyang and returned the bundle sealed as before.

sentences.zh: 世稱廉信。

translations.literal: The age called him honest and faithful.
translations.idiomatic: Men praised his honesty.

sentences.zh: 曆東荊州司馬，轉長史，帶義陽太守，領戍。

translations.literal: He held in succession Military Secretary of Eastern Jingzhou, then Chief Clerk, concurrently Governor of Yiyang, commanding the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was Military Secretary then Chief Clerk of Eastern Jingzhou, concurrently Governor of Yiyang, commanding the garrison.

sentences.zh: 雅有恤人之志。

translations.literal: He elegantly had a will to pity people.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for compassion.

sentences.zh: 再轉汝陽太守。

translations.literal: Again transferred Governor of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Governor of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 遇水澇人饑，上表請輕租賦。

translations.literal: Meeting flood and famine he memorialized asking to lighten land tax.
translations.idiomatic: Floods brought famine; he asked to lighten taxes.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，遂敕汝陽一郡，聽以小絹為調。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it and then ordered the whole commandery of Ruyang permitted to pay tribute in small silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and let all Ruyang pay tribute in light silk.

sentences.zh: 除平原相。

translations.literal: He was made Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Administrator of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 徵為征虜將軍、太中大夫，未發，卒於郡。

translations.literal: Summoned as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Grand Master of Palace Counsel — before he set out he died in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, he died in office before departing.

sentences.zh: 贈後將軍、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously Rear General and Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Rear General and Governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 子子馥，字元穎，早有學行，累遷平原相。

translations.literal: His son Zifu, styled Yuanying, early had learning and conduct, and rose through posts to Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zifu, styled Yuanying, was learned early and rose to Administrator of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 父子並為此郡，吏人懷安之。

translations.literal: Father and son both held this commandery; officials and people cherished and were at ease with them.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both governed Pingyuan; the people loved them.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，子馥不從。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang Zifu did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang Zifu would not follow.

sentences.zh: 莊帝反政，封三門縣男。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang restored the government he was enfeoffed Baron of Sanmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to power he was made Baron of Sanmen.

sentences.zh: 天平中，除太尉府司馬。

translations.literal: In Tianping he was made Military Secretary of the Grand Preceptor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping he was Military Secretary of the Grand Preceptor's Office.

sentences.zh: 白山連接三齊，瑕丘數州之界，多有賊盜。

translations.literal: White Mountain linked the three Qi; on the borders of several prefectures around Xiaqiu there were many bandits.
translations.idiomatic: White Mountain linked the three Qi; around Xiaqiu bandits were many.

sentences.zh: 子馥受使檢覆，因辨山谷要害宜立鎮戍之所。

translations.literal: Zifu received orders to inspect; he thereby distinguished valleys and passes where garrisons should stand.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to inspect, he mapped passes where garrisons should stand.

sentences.zh: 又諸州豪右。

translations.literal: Also the powerful families of the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial magnates as well

sentences.zh: 在山鼓鑄，奸黨多依之，又得密造兵仗。

translations.literal: cast metal in the mountains; many villainous factions relied on them and could also secretly forge weapons.
translations.idiomatic: smelted in the hills; outlaws clustered there and secretly forged weapons.

sentences.zh: 上表請破罷諸冶。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to break up and abolish all smelting works.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to shut every illicit foundry.

sentences.zh: 朝廷善而從之。

translations.literal: The court approved and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 後卒于清河太守。

translations.literal: Later he died in office as Administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died as Administrator of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 子馥以《三傳》經同說異，遂總為一部，傳注並出，校比短長。

translations.literal: His son Zifu, because the Three Commentaries shared one canon yet differed in interpretation, therefore compiled them into one work, with both classic and commentary presented together, comparing their lengths and merits.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zifu, finding the Three Commentaries one canon yet divergent in gloss, compiled them into a single work with text and commentary together, comparing length and merit.

sentences.zh: 會亡，未就。

translations.literal: He happened to die before it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: He died before the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 韋閬，字友觀，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Wei Lang, styled Youguan, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lang, styled Youguan, came from Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 世為三輔冠族。

translations.literal: For generations his house had been a leading clan of the Three Metropolises.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his house ranked among the leading clans of the Three Metropolises.

sentences.zh: 祖楷，晉長樂清河二郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kai had been Administrator of Changle and Qinghe in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kai had been Administrator of Changle and Qinghe under Jin.

sentences.zh: 父逵，慕容垂大長秋卿。

translations.literal: His father Kui had been Grand Chamberlain for Ceremonials under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kui had been Grand Chamberlain for Ceremonials under Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 閬少有器望，遇慕容氏政亂，避地薊城。

translations.literal: Lang in youth had talent and reputation; when the Murong regime fell into disorder he took refuge at Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lang in youth had talent and standing; when the Murong house fell into disorder he took refuge at Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 太武初，徵拜咸陽太守，轉武都太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Taiwu's reign he was summoned and appointed Administrator of Xianyang, then transferred to Administrator of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiwu's reign he was summoned as Administrator of Xianyang, then transferred to Wudu.

sentences.zh: 卒郡。

translations.literal: He died in his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子范，試守華山郡，賜爵高平男。

translations.literal: His son Fan, on probation as Administrator of Huashan Commandery, was granted the rank Baron of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan, acting Administrator of Huashan, was enfeoffed Baron of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 範子俊，字穎超，早有學。

translations.literal: Fan's son Jun, styled Yingchao, was early accomplished in learning.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's son Jun, styled Yingchao, was early accomplished in scholarship.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事祖母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his grandmother and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he served his grandmother and was famed for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 性溫和廉讓，為州裏所稱。

translations.literal: Gentle, mild, modest, and yielding, he was praised throughout the province.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle, mild, modest, and yielding, he was praised in his province.

sentences.zh: 太和中，襲爵。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he inherited the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 歷位都水使者。

translations.literal: He held the post of Commissioner of the Waters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Commissioner of the Waters.

sentences.zh: 宣武崩，領軍於忠矯擅威刑，俊與左僕射郭祚昏嫁，故亦同時遇害。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu died, the commander Yu Zhong perverted justice and wielded punishments arbitrarily; Jun, through marriage ties with Left Vice Director Guo Zuo, was therefore killed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanwu died, Commander Yu Zhong twisted justice and wielded punishments at will; Jun, allied by marriage to Left Vice Director Guo Zuo, fell with him.

sentences.zh: 臨終，訴枉于尚書元欽，欽知而不敢申理。

translations.literal: At the end he appealed his innocence to the Masters of Writing Yuan Qin; Qin knew the truth yet dared not set it right.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he appealed his innocence to Yuan Qin of the Masters of Writing; Qin knew yet dared not act.

sentences.zh: 俊歎曰：「吾一生為善，未蒙善報；

translations.literal: Jun sighed and said, "All my life I have done good, yet never received good's reward;
translations.idiomatic: Jun sighed, "All my life I did good, yet never tasted good's reward;

sentences.zh: 常不為惡，今為惡終，悠悠蒼天，抱直無訴！

translations.literal: I have never done evil, yet now evil is my end. O vast Heaven above—where shall the upright turn who have no voice?"
translations.idiomatic: I never did evil, yet evil is my end. O vast Heaven—where shall the upright cry out?"

sentences.zh: 」時人咸怨傷焉。

translations.literal: All who heard it grieved and were wounded in heart.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it grieved.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年，追贈洛州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiping he was posthumously made Inspector of Luozhou with the posthumous title Upright.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiping year 1 he was posthumously Inspector of Luozhou, posthumous title Upright.

sentences.zh: 子子粲。

translations.literal: His son was Zican.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son Zican.

sentences.zh: 子粲字暉茂。

translations.literal: Zican, styled Huimao.
translations.idiomatic: Zican was styled Huimao.
