sentences.zh: 齊王蕭寶夤為雍州刺史，引為府主簿，轉錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin was made Inspector of Yong Province, he was brought in as chief clerk of the headquarters, then promoted Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin became Inspector of Yong, Zican entered as chief headquarters clerk, then Recorder.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤反，子粲與弟子爽執志不從，相率逃免。

translations.literal: When Baoyin rebelled, Zican and his nephew Shuang held firm and would not follow, and together they fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled, Zican and his nephew Shuang held firm, refused to follow, and fled together.

sentences.zh: 雍州平，賜爵長安子。

translations.literal: When Yong Province was pacified, he was granted the rank Viscount of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong was pacified he was enfeoffed Viscount of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Putai era he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Putai he rose to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝入關，子粲曆行台左丞、南汾州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the passes, Zican successively held the posts of Left Director of the Mobile Office and Inspector of South Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu entered the passes, Zican served as Left Director of the Mobile Office and Inspector of South Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 少弟道諧為鎮城都督。

translations.literal: His youngest brother Daoxie was Garrison Commander of Zhencheng.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest brother Daoxie was Garrison Commander of Zhencheng.

sentences.zh: 元象中，齊神武命將出討，子粲及道諧俱被獲，送于晉陽。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era, Qi Shenwu ordered generals out on campaign; Zican and Daoxie were both captured and sent to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxiang, Northern Qi Shenwu sent armies forth; Zican and Daoxie were captured and sent to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 子粲累遷南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Zican was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zican rose to Inspector of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，封西僰縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Northern Qi Tianbao he was enfeoffed Baron of Xibo county.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Qi Tianbao he was enfeoffed Baron of Xibo.

sentences.zh: 後卒于豫州刺史，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: Later he died as Inspector of Yuzhou with the posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died as Inspector of Yuzhou, posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子粲兄弟十三人，並有孝行，居父喪，毀瘠過禮。

translations.literal: Zican and his twelve brothers all practiced filial devotion; in mourning for their father they wasted away beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zican and twelve brothers all practiced filial piety; mourning their father, they wasted away beyond the rites.

sentences.zh: 既葬，廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: After the burial they dwelt in huts beside the tomb and carried earth until a mound was formed.
translations.idiomatic: After burial they lodged beside the tomb and heaped earth into a mound.

sentences.zh: 弟榮亮最知名。

translations.literal: His younger brother Rongliang was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Rongliang was the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 榮亮字子昱。

translations.literal: Rongliang, styled Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: Rongliang was styled Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 博學有文才，德行仁孝，為時所重。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and gifted in letters, humane in conduct and filial in devotion, he was esteemed by his age.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and literary, humane and filial, he was esteemed in his time.

sentences.zh: 曆諫議大夫、衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Remonstrator and Grand General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was Remonstrator and Grand General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈河州刺史。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Inspector of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Inspector of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 子綱，字世紀，有操行，才學見稱，領袖本州，謂為中正。

translations.literal: His son Gang, styled Shiji, had moral resolve; his talent and learning won praise, and he led his native province—men called him the Impartial Judge.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gang, styled Shiji, had moral fiber; talent and learning won praise, and he led his province—men called him the Impartial Judge.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，位趙州長史。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he held the post of Chief Clerk of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaihuang he was Chief Clerk of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有子文宗、文英，並知名。

translations.literal: He had sons Wenzong and Wenying, both well known.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Wenzong and Wenying, both renowned.

sentences.zh: 閬從叔道福，父羆，為苻堅丞相王猛所器重，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Lang's younger cousin by the father's line, Daofu—Daofu's father Pi had been prized by Fu Jian's chancellor Wang Meng, who gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's agnatic cousin Daofu: Daofu's father Pi was prized by Wang Meng, Fu Jian's chancellor, who gave him a daughter.

sentences.zh: 仕堅為東海太守。

translations.literal: Serving Fu Jian, he was Administrator of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he was Administrator of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 堅滅，奔江左，仕宋為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian fell, he fled to the south and served Song as Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian fell he fled south and served Song as Inspector of Qin.

sentences.zh: 道福有志略，仕宋位盱眙、南沛二郡太守，領鎮北府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Daofu had will and strategy; in Song he reached the posts of Administrator of Xuyi and South Pei and Recorder of the Pacify-the-North Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu had will and strategy; in Song he was Administrator of Xuyi and South Pei and Recorder of the Pacify-the-North Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 與徐州刺史薛安都謀擁州內附，賜爵高密侯，因家彭城。

translations.literal: With Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andu he plotted to bring the province within the fold; he was granted the rank Marquis of Gaomi and made his home in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: With Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andu he plotted to submit the province; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Gaomi and settled in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兗州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Yanzhou with the posthumous title Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously Inspector of Yanzhou, posthumous title Simple.

sentences.zh: 子欣宗，以歸國勳，別賜爵杜縣侯。

translations.literal: His son Xinzong, for merit in returning to the state, was separately granted the rank Marquis of Du county.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xinzong, for merit in returning to the realm, was separately enfeoffed Marquis of Du.

sentences.zh: 歷位太中大夫、行幽州事。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Grand Master of Palace Counsel and acting Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was Grand Master of Palace Counsel and acting Inspector of You.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈南兗州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of South Yanzhou with the posthumous title Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously Inspector of South Yanzhou, posthumous title Simple.

sentences.zh: 閬從子崇，字洪基。

translations.literal: Lang's cousin Chong, styled Hongji.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's cousin Chong was styled Hongji.

sentences.zh: 父肅，字道壽，隨劉義真度江，位豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Su, styled Daoshou, had crossed the river with Liu Yizhen and held the post of Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Su, styled Daoshou, crossed the river with Liu Yizhen and was Inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 崇年十歲，父卒，母鄭氏攜以入魏，因寓居河、洛。

translations.literal: Chong was ten when his father died; his mother Lady Zheng brought him into Wei, and they lodged in the Yellow and Luo region.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was ten when his father died; Lady Zheng brought him into Wei and they settled between the Yellow and Luo.

sentences.zh: 少為舅兗州刺史鄭羲所器賞。

translations.literal: In youth he was prized and admired by his maternal uncle, Inspector of Yanzhou Zheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In youth his maternal uncle, Yanzhou Inspector Zheng Yi, prized him.

sentences.zh: 位司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: He held the post of Attendant in the Secretariat of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was Attendant in the Secretariat of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 孝文納其女為充華嬪，除南潁川太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen took his daughter as a Worthy Lady of the Inner Palace, Chong was made Administrator of South Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen took his daughter as Worthy Lady, Chong was made Administrator of South Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 不好發擿細事，恆云：「何用小察，以傷大道？

translations.literal: He did not like to pursue petty matters and would often say, "Why use small scrutiny to wound the great Way?"
translations.idiomatic: He disliked petty prosecutions and often said, "Why wound the great Way with small scrutiny?"

sentences.zh: 」吏人感之，郡中大安。

translations.literal: Officials and people were moved by him, and the commandery knew great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people were moved; the commandery knew great peace.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉賞，賜帛二百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and commended him, granting two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and commended him, granting two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，以崇為司州中正。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, Chong was made Impartial Judge of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the move to Luoyang, Chong was Impartial Judge of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋除咸陽王禧開府從事中郎，復為河南邑中正。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Attendant in the Secretariat of Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi, then again Impartial Judge of Henan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Attendant in Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi's secretariat, then again Impartial Judge of Henan.

sentences.zh: 崇頻居衡品，以平直見稱。

translations.literal: Chong repeatedly held rating offices and was praised for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Chong repeatedly held rating offices and was praised for fairness.

sentences.zh: 出為鄉郡太守，更滿應代，吏人詣闕乞留，復延三年。

translations.literal: Sent out as Administrator of Xiang Commandery, when his term ended and he should have been replaced, officials and people went to court begging that he remain; his term was extended three years.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as Administrator of Xiang, at term's end officials and people begged the court to keep him; his term was extended three years.

sentences.zh: 後卒。

translations.literal: Later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died.

sentences.zh: 子猷之，釋褐奉朝請，轉給事中、步兵校尉，稍遷前、後將軍，太中大夫，卒。

translations.literal: His son Youzhi, on first appointment Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience, then Gentleman of the Secretariat and Colonel of Footsoldiers, was gradually promoted Rear and Front General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Son Youzhi entered as Court Gentleman, rose through Gentleman of the Secretariat and Colonel of Footsoldiers to Rear and Front General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, then died.

sentences.zh: 猷之弟休之，貞和自守，未嘗言行忤物。

translations.literal: Youzhi's younger brother Xiuzhi was upright and self-contained and never spoke or acted against others.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Xiuzhi was upright and reserved, never giving offense in word or deed.

sentences.zh: 歷位給事中、河南邑中正、安西將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Gentleman of the Secretariat, Impartial Judge of Henan Commandery, General Who Pacifies the West, and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was Gentleman of the Secretariat, Impartial Judge of Henan, General Who Pacifies the West, and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子道建、道儒。

translations.literal: His sons Daojian and Daoru.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Daojian and Daoru.

sentences.zh: 閬族弟珍，字靈智，孝文賜名焉。

translations.literal: Lang's cousin Zhen, styled Lingzhi—Emperor Xiaowen granted him the name.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Zhen, styled Lingzhi—Xiaowen granted the name.

sentences.zh: 父子尚，字文叔。

translations.literal: Zhen's father Shang, styled Wenshu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's father Shang was styled Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 位樂安王良安西府從事中郎。

translations.literal: He held the post of Attendant in the Secretariat of Prince of Le'an Yuan Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was Attendant in Prince of Le'an Yuan Liang's secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 珍少有志操，歷位尚書南部郎。

translations.literal: Zhen in youth had moral resolve and held the post of Gentleman of the Southern Department in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen in youth had resolve and was Gentleman of the Southern Department.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，蠻首桓誕歸款，朝廷思安邊之略，以誕為東荊州刺史，令珍為使，與誕招慰蠻左。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaowen's reign the barbarian chief Huan Dan submitted; the court, seeking a policy to settle the frontier, made Dan Inspector of East Jingzhou and Zhen envoy to win over the barbarians of the left with him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaowen's reign the barbarian chief Huan Dan submitted; the court made Dan Inspector of East Jing and Zhen envoy to win the left-hand tribes with him.

sentences.zh: 珍至桐柏山，窮淮源，宣揚恩澤，莫不懷附。

translations.literal: Zhen reached Mount Tongbai, traced the Huai to its source, and proclaimed grace and favor—none failed to submit in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen reached Mount Tongbai, traced the Huai to its source, and proclaimed imperial grace—every tribe submitted in heart.

sentences.zh: 淮源舊有祠堂，蠻俗恆用人祭之。

translations.literal: At the Huai's source there had been a shrine where barbarian custom regularly used human sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At the Huai's source stood a shrine where barbarian custom offered human victims.

sentences.zh: 珍乃曉告曰：「天地明靈，即人之父母，豈有父母，甘子肉味？

translations.literal: Zhen then instructed them, saying, "Heaven and earth, bright in spirit, are mankind's parents—would any parent relish the taste of a child's flesh?
translations.idiomatic: Zhen instructed them: "Heaven and earth in their brightness are our parents—what parent savors a child's flesh?

sentences.zh: 自今宜悉以酒脯代用。

translations.literal: From now on you should all use wine and dried meat instead."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth use only wine and dried meat."

sentences.zh: 」群蠻從約，自此而改。

translations.literal: The tribes obeyed the covenant, and from that time the custom was changed.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes obeyed; the custom changed from that day.

sentences.zh: 凡所招降七萬餘戶，置郡縣而還。

translations.literal: In all he won over more than seventy thousand households, established commanderies and counties, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He won over more than seventy thousand households, established commanderies and counties, and returned.

sentences.zh: 以奉使稱旨，賜爵霸城子。

translations.literal: Because his mission answered the imperial will, he was granted the rank Viscount of Bacheng.
translations.idiomatic: For a mission that pleased the throne he was enfeoffed Viscount of Bacheng.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Later, for military merit, his rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for military merit, he was advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 累遷顯武將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of Manifest Martiality and Inspector of Ying.

sentences.zh: 所在有聲績，朝廷嘉之，遷龍驤將軍，賜驊騮二匹，帛五十匹，穀三百斛。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he won reputation for achievement, and the court commended him, promoting him to General of the Dragon Charger and granting two piebald horses, fifty bolts of silk, and three hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he left a record of merit; the court promoted him to General of the Dragon Charger and granted two piebald horses, fifty bolts of silk, and three hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 珍乃召集州內孤貧者，謂曰：「天子謂我能撫綏卿等，故賜以穀帛，吾何敢獨當。

translations.literal: Zhen then summoned the destitute and orphaned of the province and said to them, "The Son of Heaven says I can soothe and settle you—hence these grants of grain and silk. How dare I keep them alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen summoned the province's destitute and orphaned and said, "The Son of Heaven says I can soothe you—hence grain and silk. How dare I keep them alone?"

sentences.zh: 」遂以所賜，悉分與之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he divided everything he had been granted among them.
translations.idiomatic: He divided the whole grant among them.

sentences.zh: 尋轉荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 與尚書盧陽烏征赭陽，為齊將垣曆生、蔡道恭所敗，免歸鄉里。

translations.literal: With Masters of Writing Lu Yangwu he campaigned against Zheyang and was defeated by Qi generals Yuan Lisheng and Cai Daogong; he was dismissed and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: With Lu Yangwu of the Masters of Writing he attacked Zheyang and was beaten by Qi generals Yuan Lisheng and Cai Daogong; dismissed, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 臨別，謂陽烏曰：「主上聖明，志吞吳會。

translations.literal: On parting he said to Yangwu, "Our lord is sage and wise and intends to swallow Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On parting he told Yangwu, "Our lord is sage and wise and means to swallow Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 用兵機要，在於上流。

translations.literal: The crux of using armies lies in the upper Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: The crux of war lies in the upper Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 若有事荊楚，恐老夫復不得停耳。

translations.literal: If affairs arise in Jing and Chu, I fear this old man may not be allowed to rest again."
translations.idiomatic: If affairs stir in Jing and Chu, I fear this old man will not rest again."

sentences.zh: 」後車駕征鄧沔，復起珍為中軍大將軍、彭城王勰長史。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage campaigned against Deng and Mian, Zhen was again raised as Grand General of the Central Army and Chief Clerk to Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor campaigned against Deng and Mian, Zhen was again Grand General of the Central Army and Chief Clerk to Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie.

sentences.zh: 鄧沔既平，試守魯陽郡。

translations.literal: When Deng and Mian were pacified, he was made acting Administrator of Luyang Commandery on probation.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng and Mian were pacified, he was acting Administrator of Luyang on probation.

sentences.zh: 孝文復南伐，路經珍郡，加中壘將軍，正太守。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen campaigned south again and passed through Zhen's commandery, he was made General of the Central Rampart and confirmed as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen marched south again and passed Zhen's commandery, he was made General of the Central Rampart and confirmed Administrator.

sentences.zh: 珍從至清水，帝曰：「朕頃戎車再駕，卿恆翼務中軍。

translations.literal: Zhen followed to Qingshui. The emperor said, "These last campaigns I have twice driven the war-chariot forth, and you have always assisted in the central army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen followed to Qingshui. The emperor said, "On these last campaigns I twice took the field, and you have always served the central army.

sentences.zh: 今日之舉，亦欲引卿同行，但三鴉險要，非卿無以守也。

translations.literal: On this expedition I also wished to bring you along, but Sanya's passes are perilous—without you they cannot be held."
translations.idiomatic: This time I wished to bring you, but Sanya's passes are perilous—without you they cannot be held."

sentences.zh: 」因敕還。

translations.literal: " He therefore ordered him to return.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered him back.

sentences.zh: 及孝文崩于行宮，秘匿而還，至珍郡，始發大諱。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen died in the traveling palace the death was kept secret on the return; only when they reached Zhen's commandery was the great mourning proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen died at the traveling palace the death was concealed until they reached Zhen's commandery, where the great mourning was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 還，除中散大夫，尋加鎮遠將軍、太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: On return he was made Grand Master of the Palace, then soon added General Who Pacifies the Distance and Staff Member in the Secretariat of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was Grand Master of the Palace, then General Who Pacifies the Distance and Staff in the Secretariat of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈本將軍、青州刺史，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given his former generalship and made Inspector of Qingzhou with the posthumous title Virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously his former generalship and Inspector of Qingzhou, posthumous title Virtuous.

sentences.zh: 長子纘，字遵彥。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zuan, styled Zunyan.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Zuan was styled Zunyan.

sentences.zh: 年十三，補中書學生。

translations.literal: At thirteen he was enrolled as a student of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he entered the Central Secretariat school.

sentences.zh: 聰敏明辯，為博士李彪所稱。

translations.literal: Clever, keen, and eloquent, he was praised by Erudite Li Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and eloquent, he was praised by Erudite Li Biao.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍御中散。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Twice promoted to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 孝文每與德學沙門談論往復，纘掌綴錄，無所遺漏，頗見知賞。

translations.literal: Whenever Xiaowen debated back and forth with virtuous scholars and Buddhist monks, Zuan took charge of collation and recording and omitted nothing—he won considerable favor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xiaowen debated with scholars and monks, Zuan recorded all and omitted nothing—he won favor.

sentences.zh: 累遷長兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Acting Left Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Acting Left Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 壽春內附，尚書令王肅出鎮揚州，請纘行，為州長史。

translations.literal: When Shouchun submitted, Minister of Education Wang Su went out to garrison Yangzhou and asked Zuan to accompany him as Chief Clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouchun submitted, Wang Su of the Masters of Writing went to Yangzhou and took Zuan as provincial Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 加平遠將軍，帶梁郡太守。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and concurrent Administrator of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was General Who Pacifies the Distance and concurrent Administrator of Liang.

sentences.zh: 肅薨，敕纘行州事。

translations.literal: When Su died, an edict ordered Zuan to act in provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Su died, Zuan was ordered to act for the province.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄代肅為州，復啟纘為長史。

translations.literal: Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng replaced Su in the province and again petitioned for Zuan as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng replaced Su and again petitioned for Zuan as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 澄出征之後，梁將姜慶真乘虛攻襲，遂據外郭。

translations.literal: After Cheng marched out, Liang general Jiang Qingzhen seized the moment to attack and occupied the outer wall of the city.
translations.idiomatic: After Cheng marched out, Liang's Jiang Qingzhen attacked and seized the outer city.

sentences.zh: 雖尋克復，纘坐免官。

translations.literal: Though it was soon recovered, Zuan was dismissed from office for the fault.
translations.idiomatic: Though soon recovered, Zuan was dismissed for the fault.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 纘弟彧，字遵慶，亦有學識。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Yu, styled Zunqing, was also accomplished in learning.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Yu, styled Zunqing, was also learned.

sentences.zh: 解褐奉朝請，稍遷平遠將軍、東豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On leaving the purple he was Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience and was gradually promoted General Who Pacifies the Distance and Inspector of East Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On first appointment he was Court Gentleman and rose to General Who Pacifies the Distance and Inspector of East Yu.

sentences.zh: 綏懷蠻左，頗得其心。

translations.literal: He soothed the barbarians of the left and won their hearts fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: He soothed the left-hand tribes and fairly won their hearts.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋田益宗子魯生、魯賢先叛父南入，數為寇掠。

translations.literal: The barbarian chief Tian Yizong's sons Lusheng and Luxian had first rebelled against their father and fled south, repeatedly raiding and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yizong's sons Lusheng and Luxian had rebelled against their father, fled south, and repeatedly raided.

sentences.zh: 自彧至州，魯生等咸箋啟修敬，不得為害。

translations.literal: From the time Yu reached the province, Lusheng and the others all sent letters of respect and could not harm the land.
translations.idiomatic: From Yu's arrival, Lusheng and the others sent letters of respect and could not harm the land.

sentences.zh: 彧以蠻俗不識禮儀，乃立太學，選諸郡生徒於州總教。

translations.literal: Because barbarian custom did not know ritual and propriety, he established a National University and chose student youths from the commanderies to teach them collectively at the provincial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the tribes ignorant of ritual, he founded a National University and gathered student youths from the commanderies to teach at the seat.

sentences.zh: 又于城北置崇武館以習武焉。

translations.literal: He also set up the Hall of Honored Martiality north of the city wall for military drill.
translations.idiomatic: North of the wall he set up the Hall of Honored Martiality for drill.

sentences.zh: 州境清肅。

translations.literal: The province's borders were cleared and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The province was cleared and orderly.

sentences.zh: 罷還，遇大將軍、京兆王繼西征，請為長史。

translations.literal: On dismissal and return he met Grand General Prince of Jingzhao Ji on a western campaign and was asked to serve as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: On return he joined Grand General Prince of Jingzhao Ji's western campaign as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼尚書，為豳、夏行台，以功封陰盤縣男。

translations.literal: Soon, in his former office concurrent with the Masters of Writing, he was made Mobile Office for Bin and Xia; for merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Yinpan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, concurrent with the Masters of Writing on the Mobile Office for Bin and Xia, he was enfeoffed Baron of Yinpan for merit.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈撫軍將軍、雍州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yongzhou with the posthumous title Literary.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yong, posthumous title Literary.

sentences.zh: 子彪襲。

translations.literal: His son Biao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Son Biao inherited.

sentences.zh: 孝莊末，為藍田太守，因仕關西。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was Administrator of Lantian and therefore entered service in the Guanxi region.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaozhuang's end he was Administrator of Lantian and entered Guanxi service.

sentences.zh: 彪弟融，以軍功賜爵長安伯。

translations.literal: Biao's younger brother Rong was granted the rank Baron of Chang'an for military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Rong was enfeoffed Baron of Chang'an for military merit.

sentences.zh: 稍遷大司馬開府司馬。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Staff Member in the Secretariat of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Staff in the Grand Marshal's secretariat.

sentences.zh: 融娶司農卿趙郡李瑾女，疑其妻與章武王景哲奸通，乃刺殺之。

translations.literal: Rong married the daughter of Minister of Agriculture Li Jin of Zhao commandery and suspected his wife of adultery with Prince of Zhangwu Yuan Jingzhe; he stabbed her to death.
translations.idiomatic: Rong married Li Jin's daughter of the Ministry of Agriculture and suspected adultery with Prince of Zhangwu Yuan Jingzhe; he stabbed her dead.

sentences.zh: 懼，亦自殺。

translations.literal: In fear he also killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In fear he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 弟朏，字遵顯，少有志業。

translations.literal: Younger brother Fei, styled Zunxian, in youth had will and enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Fei, styled Zunxian, had will and enterprise in youth.

sentences.zh: 年十八，辟州主簿。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was summoned as chief clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was summoned as provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時屬歲儉，朏以家粟造粥，以飼饑人，所活甚眾。

translations.literal: It happened to be a year of scarcity; Fei used the household's grain to make porridge and fed the hungry—very many lived because of him.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of scarcity he used household grain for porridge and fed the hungry—very many lived.

sentences.zh: 解褐太學博士。

translations.literal: On leaving the purple he was Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: On first appointment he was Erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 稍遷右軍將軍，為荊、郢和糴大使。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted General of the Right Army and Commissioner for Harmonious Grain Purchase in Jing and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Right Army and Commissioner for Harmonious Grain Purchase in Jing and Ying.

sentences.zh: 南郢州刺史田夷啟稱朏父珍往任荊州，恩洽夷夏，乞朏充南道別將，領荊州驍勇，共為腹背。

translations.literal: Inspector of South Yingzhou Tian Yi memorialized that Fei's father Zhen, in his former post in Jingzhou, had won the affections of barbarians and Chinese alike, and begged that Fei be made Separate Commander of the Southern Route with Jingzhou's fierce troops to act as mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: South Ying Inspector Tian Yi memorialized that Fei's father Zhen in Jing had won barbarian and Chinese alike, and begged Fei as Separate Commander of the Southern Route with Jing's fierce troops for mutual support.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，行南荊州事。

translations.literal: Before long he was acting in South Jingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was acting in South Jing affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of East Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of East Xu.

sentences.zh: 梁遣其郢州刺史田粗憘率眾來寇，朏于石羊岡破斬之，以功封杜縣子。

translations.literal: Liang sent its Inspector of Yingzhou Tian Cuchou at the head of troops to invade; Fei on Shiyang Hill defeated and beheaded him, and for merit was enfeoffed Viscount of Du.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Ying Inspector Tian Cuchou invaded; Fei on Shiyang Hill defeated and beheaded him and was enfeoffed Viscount of Du.

sentences.zh: 卒於侍中、雍州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died as Attendant and Inspector of Yongzhou with the posthumous title Manifest.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Attendant and Inspector of Yong, posthumous title Manifest.

sentences.zh: 長子鴻，字道衍，頗有幹用，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: His eldest son Hong, styled Daoyan, had considerable ability and was repeatedly promoted Central Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Hong, styled Daoyan, had ability and rose to Central Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 天平三年，坐漏泄，賜死於家。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianping, for leaking secrets, he was granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year 3, for leaking secrets, he was granted death at home.

sentences.zh: 杜銓，字士衡，京兆人，晉征南將軍預五世孫也。

translations.literal: Du Quan, styled Shiheng, was a man of Jingzhao and fifth-generation descendant of Jin's General Who Conquers the South Du Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Du Quan, styled Shiheng, was of Jingzhao, fifth-generation descendant of Jin's General Who Conquers the South Du Yu.

sentences.zh: 祖胄，苻堅太尉長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhou had been Chief Clerk to Fu Jian's Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Zhou was Chief Clerk to Fu Jian's Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 父嶷，慕容垂秘書監，仍僑居趙郡。

translations.literal: His father Yi had been Secretary Supervisor under Murong Chui and afterward lodged in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Father Yi was Secretary Supervisor under Murong Chui and afterward lodged in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 銓學涉，有長者風，與盧玄、高允等同被徵為中書博士。

translations.literal: Quan was broadly learned and had the bearing of an elder; with Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, and the like he was summoned together as Erudite of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was broadly learned with an elder's bearing; with Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, and others he was summoned as Central Secretariat Erudite.

sentences.zh: 初，密太后父豹喪在濮陽，太武欲令迎葬於鄴，謂司徒崔浩曰：「天下諸杜，何處望高？

translations.literal: Earlier, Empress Dowager Mi's father Bao had died in Puyang; Emperor Taiwu wished to have him brought for burial at Ye and said to Minister of Education Cui Hao, "Of all the Du houses under Heaven, which is most eminent?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Empress Dowager Mi's father Bao lay dead in Puyang; Taiwu wished to bring him for burial at Ye and asked Cui Hao, "Of all the Du houses, which is most eminent?

sentences.zh: 朕今方改葬外祖，意欲取杜中長老一人，以為宗正，令營護凶事。

translations.literal: I am now about to rebury my maternal grandfather and wish to take one elder of the Du clan as Director of the Imperial Clan to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: I am reburying my maternal grandfather and wish one elder Du as Director of the Imperial Clan to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「京兆為美。

translations.literal: Hao said, "Jingzhao is finest.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Jingzhao is finest.

sentences.zh: 中書博士杜銓，其家今在趙郡，是杜預後，於今為諸杜最。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Erudite Du Quan—his family is now in Zhao commandery; he is descendant of Du Yu and among all the Du today is foremost."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Du Quan—his family is in Zhao commandery; he is Du Yu's descendant and foremost among the Du today."

sentences.zh: 」密召見，銓器貌瑰雅，太武感悅，謂浩曰：「此真吾所欲也。

translations.literal: Secretly summoned and seen, Quan's bearing was magnificent and elegant; Emperor Taiwu was moved and pleased and said to Hao, "This is truly the man I want."
translations.idiomatic: Secretly summoned, Quan's bearing was magnificent; Taiwu was pleased and told Hao, "This is truly the man I want."

sentences.zh: 」以為宗正，令與杜超子道生送豹喪柩，致葬鄴南。

translations.literal: He was made Director of the Imperial Clan and ordered, with Du Chao's son Daosheng, to escort Bao's coffin and bury him south of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Imperial Clan and, with Du Chao's son Daosheng, escorted Bao's coffin for burial south of Ye.

sentences.zh: 銓遂與超如親。

translations.literal: Quan thereafter treated Chao as kin.
translations.idiomatic: Quan thereafter treated Chao as kin.

sentences.zh: 超謂銓曰：「既是宗近，何緣僑居趙郡？

translations.literal: Chao said to Quan, "We are close in the clan—why lodge in Zhao commandery?"
translations.idiomatic: Chao said, "We are close kin—why lodge in Zhao?"

sentences.zh: 」乃延引同屬魏郡。

translations.literal: He therefore drew him in and settled him in the same lineage in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He drew him in to the same lineage in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 再遷中書侍郎，賜爵新豐侯。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and granted the rank Marquis of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Twice promoted to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and enfeoffed Marquis of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈相州刺史、魏縣侯，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Xiangzhou and Marquis of Wei county with the posthumous title Manifest.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously Inspector of Xiang and Marquis of Wei, posthumous title Manifest.

sentences.zh: 子振，字季元。

translations.literal: His son Zhen, styled Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhen was styled Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，卒于中書博士。

translations.literal: Recommended as Outstanding Talent, he died as Erudite of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Outstanding Talent, he died as Central Secretariat Erudite.

sentences.zh: 振子遇，字慶期，位尚書起部郎。

translations.literal: Zhen's son Yu, styled Qingqi, held the post of Gentleman of the Ministry of Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's son Yu, styled Qingqi, was Gentleman of the Ministry of Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 竊官材瓦起立私宅，清論鄙之。

translations.literal: He appropriated official timber and tiles to build a private residence; men of pure judgment despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He took official timber and tiles for a private house; pure judges despised him.

sentences.zh: 卒于河東太守，贈都官尚書、豫州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: He died as Administrator of Hedong and was posthumously made Director of the Ministry of Justice and Inspector of Yuzhou with the posthumous title Kind.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Administrator of Hedong; posthumously Director of the Ministry of Justice and Inspector of Yu, posthumous title Kind.

sentences.zh: 銓族孫景，字宣明，學通經史。

translations.literal: Quan's agnatic cousin Jing, styled Xuanming, was learned and versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Jing, styled Xuanming, was versed in classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 州府交辟，不就。

translations.literal: Provincial and prefectural offices repeatedly summoned him, but he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and prefectures repeatedly summoned him; he would not go.

sentences.zh: 景子裕，字慶延，雖官非貴仕，而文學相傳。

translations.literal: Jing's son Yu, styled Yanqing, though his offices were not lofty, passed literature from hand to hand.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's son Yu, styled Yanqing, held no lofty office yet literature passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，位止樂陵令。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, he reached only Magistrate of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he reached only Magistrate of Leling.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，退居教授，終於家。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he retired to teach and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he retired to teach and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子正玄，字知禮，少傳家業，耽志經史。

translations.literal: His son Zhengxuan, styled Zhili, in youth inherited the family craft and devoted himself to the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhengxuan, styled Zhili, inherited the family craft and devoted himself to classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇十五年，舉秀才，試策高第。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kaihuang he was recommended as Outstanding Talent and ranked high in the policy examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 15 he was recommended as Outstanding Talent and ranked high in the policy examination.

sentences.zh: 曹司以策過左僕射楊素，怒曰：「周孔更生，尚不得為秀才，刺史何忽妄舉此人？

translations.literal: The ministry clerks, because the policy essay surpassed Left Vice Director Yang Su, said in anger, "If Zhou and Confucius were reborn they still could not be Outstanding Talent—why does the inspector rashly recommend this man?
translations.idiomatic: Clerks, because the essay surpassed Left Vice Director Yang Su, said angrily, "If Zhou and Confucius were reborn they could not be Outstanding Talent—why does the inspector rashly recommend this man?

sentences.zh: 可附下考。

translations.literal: He should be given the lowest annual rating."
translations.idiomatic: Give him the lowest annual rating."

sentences.zh: 」乃以策抵地，不視。

translations.literal: They dashed the essay to the ground and would not look at it.
translations.idiomatic: They dashed the essay to the ground unread.

sentences.zh: 時海內唯正玄一人應秀才，余常貢者，隨例銓注訖，正玄獨不得進止。

translations.literal: At that time within the realm only Zhengxuan alone had answered the Outstanding Talent summons; the rest of the regular tribute candidates were registered and dismissed as usual, but Zhengxuan alone could neither advance nor withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Within the realm only Zhengxuan had answered the Outstanding Talent summons; regular tribute candidates were registered and dismissed, but Zhengxuan alone could neither advance nor leave.

sentences.zh: 曹司以選期將盡，重以啟素。

translations.literal: The ministry clerks, because the selection period was nearly over, again reported to Su.
translations.idiomatic: Because the selection period was nearly over, the clerks again reported to Su.

sentences.zh: 素志在試退正玄，乃手題使擬司馬相如《上林賦》、王褒《聖主得賢臣頌》、班固《燕然山銘》、張載《劍閣銘》、《白鸚鵡賦》，曰：「我不能為君住宿，可至未進令就。

translations.literal: Su's intent was to test and dismiss Zhengxuan, so he himself set topics requiring drafts after Sima Xiangru's "Shanglin Fu," Wang Bao's "The Sage Lord Obtains Worthy Ministers," Ban Gu's "Yanshan Mountain Inscription," Zhang Zai's "Sword Pass Inscription" and "White Parrot Fu," saying, "I cannot lodge you overnight—you may come before dismissal is final and finish at once."
translations.idiomatic: Su meant to test and dismiss him, set topics requiring drafts of Xiangru's "Shanglin Fu," Wang Bao's "Sage Lord" hymn, Ban Gu's "Yanshan Inscription," Zhang Zai's "Sword Pass" and "White Parrot" pieces, saying, "I cannot lodge you—come before dismissal is final and finish at once."

sentences.zh: 」正玄及時並了。

translations.literal: Zhengxuan finished all at once on time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengxuan finished all at once on time.

sentences.zh: 素讀數遍，大驚曰：「誠好秀才！

translations.literal: Su read them several times over and said in great astonishment, "Truly a fine Outstanding Talent!"
translations.idiomatic: Su read them through and cried, "Truly a fine Outstanding Talent!"

sentences.zh: 」命曹司錄奏。

translations.literal: He ordered the ministry clerks to record and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the clerks to record and memorialize.

sentences.zh: 屬吏部選期已過，注色令還。

translations.literal: It happened that the Ministry of Personnel selection period had passed; they noted his name and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel selection period had passed; they noted his name and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 期年重集，素謂曹司曰：「秀才杜正玄至。

translations.literal: A year later they assembled again; Su said to the clerks, "Outstanding Talent Du Zhengxuan has come."
translations.idiomatic: A year later they assembled again; Su told the clerks, "Outstanding Talent Du Zhengxuan has come."

sentences.zh: 」又試《官人有奇器》闕並立成，文不加點。

translations.literal: They again tested him on the "Ballad of the Official's Rare Vessel" and he completed it standing, the text without a single correction.
translations.idiomatic: They again tested the "Ballad of the Official's Rare Vessel"; he completed it standing, without a single correction.

sentences.zh: 素大嗟之，命吏部優敘。

translations.literal: Su sighed greatly in admiration and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to give him preferential ranking.
translations.idiomatic: Su sighed in admiration and ordered preferential ranking.

sentences.zh: 曹司以擬長寧王記室參軍。

translations.literal: The clerks proposed him as Recorder to Prince of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks proposed Recorder to Prince of Changning.

sentences.zh: 時素情背曹官，及見，曰：「小王不盡其才也。

translations.literal: At that time Su's feelings turned against the ministry officials; when he saw the proposal he said, "The young prince does not exhaust this man's talent."
translations.idiomatic: Su had turned against the ministry; seeing the proposal he said, "The young prince does not exhaust this man's talent."

sentences.zh: 」晉王廣方鎮揚州，妙選府僚，乃以正玄為晉王府參軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang was then garrisoning Yangzhou and choosing headquarters staff with care; Zhengxuan was therefore made Staff Member to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Yang Guang was garrisoning Yangzhou and choosing staff with care; Zhengxuan was made Staff to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 後豫章王鎮揚州，又為豫章王記室。

translations.literal: Later when Prince of Yuzhang garrisoned Yangzhou, he again served as Recorder to the Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Prince of Yuzhang garrisoned Yangzhou, he was Recorder to the Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 正玄弟正藏，字為善，亦好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Zhengxuan's younger brother Zhengcang, styled Weishan, also loved learning and was skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Zhengcang, styled Weishan, also loved learning and composition.

sentences.zh: 開皇十六年，舉秀才。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaihuang he was recommended as Outstanding Talent.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 16 he was recommended as Outstanding Talent.

sentences.zh: 時蘇威監選，試擬賈誼《過秦論》及《尚書湯誓》、《匠人箴》、《連理樹賦》、《幾賦》、《弓銘》，應時並就，又無點竄。

translations.literal: At that time Su Wei supervised the selection; the test required drafts of Jia Yi's "On the Qin," the "Pledge of Tang" from the Documents, the "Artificer's Maxim," the "Intertwined Trees Fu," the "Table Fu," and the "Bow Inscription"—he finished all on time, again without emendation.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei supervised selection; the test required Jia Yi's "On the Qin," the Documents' "Pledge of Tang," the "Artificer's Maxim," "Intertwined Trees," "Table," and "Bow" pieces—he finished on time without emendation.

sentences.zh: 時射策甲第者合奏，曹司難為別奏，抑為乙科。

translations.literal: At that time those who ranked first class in the archery-policy examination were to be memorialized together; the clerks found it hard to memorialize separately and demoted him to second class.
translations.idiomatic: First-class archery-policy candidates were memorialized together; clerks found separate memorial hard and demoted him to second class.

sentences.zh: 正藏訴屈，威怒，改為丙第，授純州行參軍。

translations.literal: Zhengcang appealed the injustice; Wei was angry and changed him to third class, appointing him Mobile Office Staff Member in Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengcang appealed; Wei was angry and changed him to third class, appointing Mobile Office Staff in Chun.

sentences.zh: 遷梁郡下邑縣正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Xiayi in Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Magistrate of Xiayi in Liang.

sentences.zh: 大業中，與劉炫同以學業該通，應詔被舉。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he and Liu Xuan were both recommended by imperial edict for comprehensive mastery of learning.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he and Liu Xuan were both recommended by edict for comprehensive learning.

sentences.zh: 時正藏弟正儀貢充進士，正倫為秀才，兄弟三人同時應命，當世嗟美之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhengcang's younger brother Zhengyi had presented himself as Presented Scholar and Zhenglun as Outstanding Talent—the three brothers answered the summons together, and the age sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhengcang's brother Zhengyi had presented himself as Presented Scholar and Zhenglun as Outstanding Talent—the three brothers answered together, and the age admired them.

sentences.zh: 著作郎王劭奏追修史，司谷大夫薛道衡奏擬從事，並以見任且放還。

translations.literal: Court Gentleman for the Imperial Compilation Wang Shao memorialized to pursue revision of the histories; Minister of Grain Xue Daohang memorialized to draft them as staff—both were in current posts and were sent home for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: Compilation Gentleman Wang Shao memorialized to revise the histories; Grain Minister Xue Daohang memorialized staff—all were in post and sent home for now.

sentences.zh: 九年，從駕征遼，為夫餘道行軍長史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed the imperial progress on the Liaodong campaign as Chief Clerk on the Fuyu Route army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he followed the Liaodong campaign as Chief Clerk on the Fuyu Route.

sentences.zh: 還至涿郡，卒。

translations.literal: On return he reached Zhuo commandery and died.
translations.idiomatic: On return he reached Zhuo commandery and died.

sentences.zh: 正藏為文迅速，有如宿構。

translations.literal: Zhengcang composed with speed, as though the text had been prepared overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengcang wrote with speed, as though prepared overnight.

sentences.zh: 曾令數人並執紙筆，各題一文，正藏口授俱成，皆有文理，為當時所異。

translations.literal: Once he had several men each hold brush and paper, each set a topic for an essay; Zhengcang dictated and all were completed at once, each with literary order—men of the time marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Once he set several men with brush and paper, each with a topic; Zhengcang dictated and all were finished at once, each ordered—his age marveled.

sentences.zh: 又為《文軌》二十卷，論為文體則，甚有條貫。

translations.literal: He also wrote Literary Tracks in twenty scrolls, discussing the norms of literary form, with very clear arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Literary Tracks in twenty scrolls on literary norms, very clearly arranged.

sentences.zh: 後生寶而行之，多資以解褐，大行於世，謂之《杜家新書》云。

translations.literal: Later students treasured and practiced it; many relied on it to leave the purple, and it spread greatly in the world—called the New Book of the Du House.
translations.idiomatic: Later students treasured it; many relied on it to leave the purple, and it spread widely—called the New Book of the Du House.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋隱操行貞白，遺略榮名；

translations.literal: The historians comment: Song Yin's conduct was pure and white, leaving glory and name behind;
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Song Yin's conduct was pure white, leaving glory behind;

sentences.zh: 宣、愔並保退素，咸見徵辟，可謂德門者矣。

translations.literal: Xuan and Yin both preserved withdrawal and simplicity and were all summoned to office—houses of virtue, indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Yin both preserved withdrawal and simplicity and were summoned to office—houses of virtue indeed.

sentences.zh: 義和以才度見知，跡參顧命，拔萃出類，當有以哉！

translations.literal: Yihe was known for talent and measure, his traces joining in entrusted counsel; standing out above the crowd—there must have been cause!
translations.idiomatic: Yihe was known for talent; his traces joined entrusted counsel; standing above the crowd—there was cause!

sentences.zh: 無子之歎，豈徒羊舌！

translations.literal: The sigh over having no son—is it only Yangshe's!
translations.idiomatic: The sigh over no son—is it only Yangshe's!

sentences.zh: 宗祀不亡，蓋其幸也。

translations.literal: That the ancestral sacrifices did not perish was perhaps their fortune.
translations.idiomatic: That ancestral sacrifice did not perish was perhaps fortune.

sentences.zh: 翻剛鯁自立，猛而斷務。

translations.literal: Fan was upright and independent, fierce in cutting through affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was upright and independent, fierce in affairs.

sentences.zh: 世良昆季，雅有家風。

translations.literal: Shiliang and his brothers, refined in family style.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang and his brothers refined the family style.

sentences.zh: 道謨卜筮取達，季良累於學淺。

translations.literal: Daomo reached eminence through divination; Jiliang was hindered by shallow learning.
translations.idiomatic: Daomo reached eminence through divination; Jiliang was weighed down by shallow learning.

sentences.zh: 刁雍才識恢遠，著聲立事，禮遇優隆，世有人爵，堂構之義也。

translations.literal: Diao Yong's talent and vision were broad and far; he won fame in founding affairs, received preferential treatment, and for generations held human rank—the meaning of building the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yong's talent was broad and far; he won fame, received honor, and for generations held rank—the meaning of building the hall.

sentences.zh: 辛、韋不殞門風。

translations.literal: The Xin and Wei houses did not let their gate's wind perish.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Wei did not let their gate's wind perish.

sentences.zh: 杜銓所在為重。

translations.literal: Wherever Du Quan stood, he was held in weight.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Du Quan stood, men gave him weight.

sentences.zh: 正玄難兄難弟，信為美哉！

translations.literal: Zhengxuan—hard to say which brother excels; truly beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Zhengxuan—hard to say which brother excels; beautiful indeed!
